recipes.title: Ahi Tuna on Crispy Rice
equipment: Cast-iron or other heavy skillet (for searing)

items: 1 cup sushi rice (short-grain), rinsed until the water runs clear
8 oz sushi-grade ahi tuna steak, about 1 inch thick, kept cold until cooking
2 Tbsp sesame seeds (white, black or a mix)
½ cup neutral oil (such as canola or avocado), divided
1 jalapeño, sliced into very thin rounds

steps: Combine the rice and 1¼ cups water in the saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 min. Rest off the heat, covered, 10 min.

Stir the vinegar, sugar and ½ tsp salt into the warm rice. While it's still warm, press it firmly into the lined pan in an even layer about ¾ inch thick, using wet hands or the bottom of a cup. Cover and chill at least 1 hr, until firm.
Lift the rice out by the plastic and cut it into 16 squares, about 2 inches each. Wipe the knife with a damp towel between cuts.

Heat ¼ cup oil in the nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Fry the squares in batches, 3–4 min per side, until deep golden and crisp, adding more oil as needed. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

Pat the tuna dry, season it with salt and press sesame seeds onto all sides. Heat 1 Tbsp oil in the heavy skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Sear the tuna 30–45 sec per side, until the seeds are toasted and only the outer ⅛ inch turns opaque.
Move the tuna to a cutting board and slice it against the grain about ¼ inch thick.
Top each rice square with a slice of avocado, a slice of tuna and a jalapeño round. Spoon a little ponzu over each and scatter with scallions. Serve right away while the rice is crisp.
tips: The tuna is served rare, so buy fish sold as sushi-grade or for raw eating. Keep it in the fridge until the minute you sear it and serve within 30 min.
Press the rice while it's warm. Cold rice won't stick together and the squares fall apart in the pan.
Make the rice block up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Fry it just before serving.
recipes.storage: Doesn't keep. The rice loses its crunch and the tuna is rare, so eat it the day you make it. Only the uncut, unfried rice block keeps, up to 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.title: Anne's Chicken Shit

items: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 2 lb), cut into 1-inch cubes
1 can (10½ oz) condensed cream of chicken soup
1 large can (6 oz) French fried onion rings, such as Durkee or French's

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 2-quart baking dish.

Bring 8 cups water to a boil in a 4-quart saucepan over high heat. Add the cubed chicken, lower to medium heat, and simmer 6 to 8 min, until the outside is white and the centers are just barely pink. Drain in a colander.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the cream of chicken soup, mayonnaise, scallions, lemon juice, salt and pepper until smooth.
Fold the drained chicken into the sauce until every piece is coated. Spread it evenly in the baking dish.
Bake uncovered 30 min, until the sauce bubbles around the edges.
Take the dish out and crunch the fried onion rings over the top with your hands, covering the chicken evenly.
Bake another 15 min, until the onions are deep golden and the chicken reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer in the thickest piece. Let it rest 5 min before serving.
tips: 1 Tbsp of pepper is what the card says and it makes a peppery dish. Start with 1 tsp if your family likes it milder.
You can use bone-in breasts, as the card notes. Cut the meat off the bone before cubing, or parboil whole and then cube.
Serve over rice or egg noodles to catch the creamy sauce.
recipes.storage: Keeps covered in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. Freezing is not recommended because the mayonnaise sauce can separate. Reheat in a 350°F oven for 15 to 20 min until hot; the onions will soften.

recipes.title: Apple Cider Pork Chops with Roasted Squash

items: 4 bone-in pork chops, about 1 inch thick
1 small butternut squash (about 2 lb), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 crisp apple (such as Honeycrisp), cored and sliced ¼ inch thick
2 Tbsp unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
Toss the squash with the oil, salt and cinnamon on the pan and spread it in a single layer. Roast 25–30 min, flipping once halfway, until fork-tender and browned at the edges.
While the squash roasts, pat the chops dry with paper towels and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the chops 4–5 min without moving them, until deep golden. Flip, lower the heat to medium and cook 4–6 min more, until they read 145°F in the thickest part away from the bone.
Move the chops to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest 3 min. Pour off all but 1 Tbsp of the fat.

Add the apple slices to the skillet over medium heat and cook 2 min, until they start to soften. Add the cider, Dijon and brown sugar, scraping up the browned bits. Boil 5–7 min, until reduced by half and syrupy.
Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the butter and thyme until the sauce is glossy. Stir in any juices from the resting plate.
Spoon the apples and sauce over the chops and serve with the squash.
tips: Buy pre-cut butternut squash to save about 10 min of prep.
Thinner chops (½ inch) need only 2–3 min per side. Check the temperature early so they don't dry out.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the chops covered in a skillet over medium-low heat with a splash of cider or water so they stay moist. Reheat the squash in a 400°F oven 8–10 min.

recipes.title: Asian Cucumber Salad

items: 2 medium cucumbers (or 1 English cucumber), sliced ⅛ inch thick

steps: Slice the cucumbers ⅛ inch thick. Toss them with 1 tsp salt in a colander set over a bowl.
Let them sit 10–15 min, until they release water and turn bendy. Shake off the liquid and pat dry with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, whisk the vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, red pepper flakes and garlic until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cucumbers and toss to coat. Taste and add a pinch of sugar if it's too sharp.
Chill 15–30 min before serving.
tips: Don't skip the salting. It pulls out water so the dressing doesn't get diluted.
For a chunkier salad that soaks up more dressing, smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife and cut into bite-size pieces instead of slicing.
Add 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds or a splash of soy sauce for more depth.
recipes.storage: Best the day it's made. It keeps 1–2 days in the fridge but softens and gets watery. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Bacon Carbonara

items: 2 tsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
6 slices bacon, cut into ½-inch pieces
2 large eggs plus 1 large yolk, at room temperature
¾ cup finely grated parmesan or pecorino romano, plus 2 Tbsp to serve
1 tsp coarsely ground black pepper, plus more to serve

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 2 tsp salt. That's less than usual because the bacon and cheese are salty.
Cook the bacon in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat 8–10 min, stirring now and then, until crisp. Turn off the heat. Spoon out all but 1 Tbsp of the fat, leaving the bacon in the pan.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, yolk, cheese and pepper until smooth.
Cook the pasta until al dente. Scoop out 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Add the hot pasta to the bacon skillet, still off the heat, and toss to coat it in the fat.
Pour in the egg mixture and ¼ cup pasta water and toss fast and nonstop with tongs until the sauce turns creamy.

Set the skillet over low heat and keep tossing 1–2 min, until the sauce thickens slightly and reads 160°F. Pull it off the moment it thickens. If it starts to look curdled, take it off the heat and add a splash of pasta water.
Serve right away topped with more cheese and pepper.
tips: Have everything ready before you drain the pasta. The sauce comes together in about 2 min and won't wait.
Use pasteurized eggs if you're cooking for someone who is pregnant, very young, older or has a weak immune system.
recipes.storage: Best eaten right away. Leftovers keep in the fridge up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a skillet over low heat with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming (165°F). Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Balsamic Asparagus and Green Beans

items: 1 bunch asparagus (about 1 lb), woody ends snapped off

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper third. Pat the green beans and asparagus dry so they char instead of steam.
In a large bowl, toss the green beans with 1 Tbsp oil and half the salt. Spread them on a rimmed sheet pan in a single layer and roast 10 min.
While they roast, toss the asparagus in the same bowl with the remaining 1 Tbsp oil, the rest of the salt and the pepper.

Add the asparagus to the pan, toss with the beans and spread everything back into a single layer. Roast 10–12 min more, until both are tender-crisp and charred in spots. Pencil-thin asparagus may need only 8 min.
Move to a platter and drizzle with the balsamic glaze.
tips: Skillet version: heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just smokes. Cook the green beans 5–6 min, add the asparagus and cook 4–5 min more, tossing now and then, until charred in spots. Work in batches if the pan is crowded.
No glaze: simmer ½ cup balsamic vinegar in a small pan over medium-low heat 8–10 min, until reduced by half. It thickens more as it cools.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot skillet 2–3 min or eat at room temperature. Add a fresh drizzle of glaze after reheating.

recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli
recipes.cook: 5–6 hr on low or 2½–3 hr on high, plus 30 min
recipes.total: 5 hr 45 min–6 hr 45 min on low (3 hr 15 min–3 hr 45 min on high)
equipment: Medium saucepan with lid (for the rice)

items: 1½ lb flank steak or boneless chuck, fully thawed, sliced ¼ inch thick against the grain
4 cups broccoli florets (about 1 large head), cut bite-size

steps: Whisk the broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and garlic in a 6-quart slow cooker until the sugar dissolves.
Add the beef and stir so every piece is covered by the sauce.
Cover and cook on low 5–6 hr or on high 2½–3 hr, until the beef is tender when pierced with a fork.
In a small bowl, stir the cornstarch into the cold water until smooth. Stir it into the slow cooker along with the broccoli.
Switch to high, cover and cook 20–30 min, until the sauce is thick and glossy and the broccoli is bright green and crisp-tender. Any longer and the broccoli turns mushy.
Meanwhile, cook the rice as the package directs. Serve the beef and broccoli over rice with sesame seeds and scallions.
tips: Freeze the steak 20 min before slicing. Firm meat is much easier to cut thin.
For crisper broccoli, microwave it covered with 2 Tbsp water 3 min and stir it in after the sauce has thickened.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave or in a skillet over medium heat until hot. The broccoli softens as it sits, so freezing isn't recommended.

recipes.title: Beef Chili with All the Toppings
recipes.cook: 6–8 hr on low or 3–4 hr on high
recipes.total: 6 hr 20 min–8 hr 20 min on low (3 hr 20 min–4 hr 20 min on high)

items: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) diced tomatoes, with their juice
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and onion and cook 8–10 min, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F. Raw ground beef should never go straight into a slow cooker.
Stir in the garlic and cook 1 min, until fragrant. Tip the pan and spoon off the extra fat.
Scrape the beef mixture into a 6-quart slow cooker. Add the beans, crushed and diced tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, salt and chipotle, if using. Stir well.
Cover and cook on low 6–8 hr or on high 3–4 hr, until thick and the flavors have blended.
Taste and add more salt if needed. If it's thicker than you like, stir in ½ cup water.
Ladle into bowls and top with avocado, sour cream, cheddar, cilantro and scallions. Serve cornbread on the side.
tips: For deeper flavor, stir the spices into the browned beef for the last 1 min in the skillet before it goes into the slow cooker.
Brown the beef the night before and refrigerate it. In the morning everything goes straight into the pot; add about 30 min to the cook time since it starts cold.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat on the stove over medium heat, stirring, until it simmers, or in the microwave until steaming.

recipes.title: Beef Stew
equipment: 6-quart Dutch oven or heavy pot with a lid

items: 2 lb boneless beef chuck roast, cut into 1½-inch cubes
3 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
2 celery ribs, cut into ½-inch slices
1 lb red potatoes, cut into 1½-inch chunks

steps: Pat the beef dry with paper towels. In a large bowl, toss it with the flour, 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper until coated.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in the Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add half the beef in a single layer with space between the pieces. Brown 4–5 min, turning, until deep brown on at least 2 sides. Move to a plate and repeat with the rest of the oil and beef. A crowded pot steams the meat instead of browning it.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 5 min, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until the onion is soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1–2 min, until the paste turns a darker red.
Pour in the broth and scrape the bottom of the pot. Return the beef and its juices, then add the thyme, bay leaf and the remaining ½ tsp salt. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer 1 hr, stirring every 20 min. Keep it at a gentle bubble; a hard boil makes the beef tough.
Add the potatoes and push them under the liquid. Cover and simmer 40–60 min more, until the potatoes are tender and the beef is fork-tender and pulls apart easily.
Remove the bay leaf and any thyme stems. Taste and add salt and pepper. For a thicker stew, simmer uncovered 10 min more.
tips: Slow cooker: do steps 1–4 in the Dutch oven, then move everything, including the raw potatoes, to a 6-quart slow cooker. Cook on low 8 hr, until the beef is fork-tender.
With white beans, like her October 2025 version: stir in 1 can (15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed, for the last 15 min.
Buy a whole chuck roast and cube it yourself. Packaged stew meat is often mixed cuts that cook unevenly.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months; the potatoes get a little grainy. Reheat in a covered pot over medium-low heat, stirring, until bubbling, and add a splash of broth if it's too thick.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Stuffed Potatoes

items: 4 medium russet potatoes (8–10 oz each), scrubbed and dried
2 cups cooked shredded chicken (about 10 oz; rotisserie works)
¼ cup ranch dressing or sour cream

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil.
Prick each potato 6–8 times with a fork. Rub with the oil and salt and set them on the pan. Bake 50–60 min, until the skins are crisp and a fork slides into the center with no resistance.
While the potatoes bake, toss the chicken with the buffalo sauce in a medium bowl until evenly coated.
Cut a slit along the top of each potato, squeeze the ends to open it and fluff the inside with a fork. Pile in the buffalo chicken and top each potato with ¼ cup cheddar.
Return the pan to the 425°F oven for 10–12 min, until the cheese is melted and bubbling and the chicken filling reads 165°F in the center.
Drizzle with the ranch or sour cream and scatter the scallions on top.
tips: Microwave shortcut: microwave the pricked potatoes 8–10 min, turning once, until tender. Then rub with oil and salt and bake at 425°F for 15 min to crisp the skins.
No cooked chicken: simmer 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts in salted water over medium-low heat 15–18 min, until they read 165°F, then shred with two forks.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days, with the ranch and scallions kept separate. Reheat at 375°F for 15–20 min or in the microwave 2–3 min, until the filling reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Burgers, Caprese or Avocado-Bacon

items: 1 slice fresh mozzarella (about 1 oz), ¼ inch thick
1 slice ripe tomato, ¼ inch thick
3 fresh basil leaves or 1 Tbsp pesto

steps: Cook the bacon in the skillet over medium heat 8–12 min, turning a few times, until crisp. Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate. Pour off all but about 1 Tbsp of the fat.

Divide the beef into 4 equal portions (6 oz each). Gently shape each into a patty ¾ inch thick and about ½ inch wider than the buns. Press a shallow thumbprint into the center so they don't puff up. Season both sides with the salt and pepper right before cooking.
Spread the butter on the cut sides of the buns. Toast them cut side down in the skillet over medium heat 1–2 min, until golden. Set aside.
Raise the heat to medium-high. Add the patties and cook 4–5 min without pressing them, until a brown crust forms. Flip.
Cook 3–4 min more. For the last minute, lay cheddar on 3 patties and the mozzarella on 1, then cover with the lid until the cheese melts. The burgers are done at 160°F in the center.
Build the caprese burger with the mozzarella patty, tomato, basil or pesto and a drizzle of balsamic glaze. Build the others with the cheddar patties, 2 slices bacon each and the avocado.
tips: Grill: heat to medium-high (about 400–450°F) and oil the grates. Cook 4–5 min per side, until 160°F.
Don't press the patties with the spatula. It squeezes out the juice and makes dry burgers.
Want ⅓-lb burgers instead: use 1⅓ lb beef for 4 patties, or make 5 from 1⅔ lb.
recipes.storage: Cooked patties keep 3–4 days in the fridge. Reheat in a covered skillet over medium-low heat 4–5 min, until hot (165°F). Store toppings separately and build the burgers fresh.

recipes.title: Burrito Bowl with Cilantro-Lime Rice

items: 2 chipotle peppers in adobo, plus 1 Tbsp of the sauce
1½ cups corn (frozen and thawed, or canned and drained)
¼ cup finely diced red onion
1 cup shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar

steps: Blend the chipotles, adobo sauce, garlic, 2 Tbsp oil, cumin and salt until smooth. Rub it all over the chicken and let it sit while you start the rice, or up to 1 hr in the fridge.
Bring the rice, 2¼ cups water and 1 tsp salt to a boil in the saucepan over high heat. Cover, turn to low and cook 15 min. Rest off the heat, covered, 10 min.

Heat the remaining 1 Tbsp oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 5–7 min per side, until charred in spots and it reads 165°F in the thickest part. Rest 5 min, then chop into bite-size pieces.
Stir the corn, red onion, cilantro, lime juice and salt together for the salsa.
Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in the lime zest, lime juice and cilantro.
Warm the beans in a small pot over medium heat or in the microwave for 2 min.
Build each bowl with rice, beans, chicken and corn salsa. Top with romaine, cheese, sour cream and guacamole.
tips: Grill the chicken over medium-high heat instead, 5–6 min per side, to 165°F.
Freeze the leftover chipotles in a zip-top bag. They keep 3 months.
For lunches, pack the rice, beans, chicken and salsa together and add the cold toppings after reheating.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the cold toppings kept separate. Cool the rice within 2 hr. Reheat rice, beans and chicken covered in the microwave 2–3 min, until hot. Guacamole browns within a day.

recipes.title: Burritos with Pico de Gallo

items: 1 cup shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese (4 oz)
1 lb ground beef (85–90% lean), or 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, rinsed and drained
1 tsp olive oil (for the bean version)
½ small white onion, finely diced
1 Tbsp fresh lime juice (about ½ lime)

steps: Make the pico. In a medium bowl, mix the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime juice and salt. Let it sit while you cook.

For beef, cook it in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat 6–8 min, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F. Spoon off the fat. For beans, heat the oil over medium heat and add the beans.

Stir in the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt and ⅓ cup water. Simmer over medium heat 2–3 min, until the liquid is mostly gone. If using beans, mash about a third of them with a spoon. Move the filling to a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Stack the tortillas between damp paper towels and microwave 30–45 sec, until soft and bendable. Warm tortillas fold without cracking.
Down the center of each tortilla, layer ½ cup rice, a quarter of the filling, ¼ cup cheese and 2–3 Tbsp pico. Lift the pico out with a slotted spoon so its juice stays behind.
Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll it up tight.
Heat the dry skillet over medium heat. Sear the burritos seam-side down 2 min, until golden and the seam holds. Turn and brown the other side 1–2 min. Serve with the rest of the pico.
tips: Make the pico up to 1 day ahead, but add the salt just before serving so it doesn't turn watery.
Don't overfill. About 1½ cups of filling is the most a 10-inch tortilla can hold and still roll.
Tater tots on the side make it a full plate.
recipes.storage: Wrap cooled burritos (without pico) in foil. Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat unwrapped in the microwave 1–2 min (3–4 min from frozen, turning halfway), or bake in the foil at 375°F for 15–20 min, until hot in the center (165°F). Pico keeps 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Butternut Squash Mac and Cheese
equipment: 2-quart metal or ceramic baking dish (not glass, since it goes under the broiler)

items: 12 oz short pasta (such as cavatappi, shells or elbows)
2 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
2 cups roasted or frozen butternut squash cubes
½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
½ cup panko or crushed pepitas

steps: If using frozen squash, microwave it covered 5–6 min, stirring once, until soft all the way through. Set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 2 Tbsp salt. Cook the pasta 1 min less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, melt 1 Tbsp butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 1 min, until fragrant. Scrape it into the blender with the squash and warm milk and blend until completely smooth.

Pour the purée back into the saucepan and warm over medium-low heat until steaming. Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time, then the parmesan, nutmeg and ½ tsp salt, until melted and smooth. Don't let it boil.
Add the pasta and stir to coat. Add pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is creamy and loose. Taste and add salt and pepper.
Turn the broiler to high. Spread the pasta in the baking dish. Toss the panko with the melted butter and scatter it over the top.
Broil 2–3 min, until the top is golden. Watch it closely. Let it sit 5 min before serving.
tips: Shred your own cheddar. Pre-shredded cheese has anti-caking powder that makes the sauce grainy.
Skip the broiler if you're short on time. Toast the buttered panko in a skillet over medium heat 2–3 min and sprinkle it on.
Stir in browned Italian sausage for more protein.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in the microwave or a saucepan over low heat with a splash of milk. Freeze up to 2 months without the topping, then thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

recipes.title: Butternut Squash Soup

items: 1 medium butternut squash (2½–3 lb), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes (about 6 cups)
⅛ tsp ground nutmeg or ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
½ cup heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk

steps: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and ½ tsp of the salt and cook 5–7 min, stirring, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Add the squash, broth, the remaining ½ tsp salt, the pepper and the nutmeg or cinnamon. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, partly cover and simmer 20–25 min, until a squash cube crushes easily against the side of the pot with a fork.

Turn off the heat. Blend with an immersion blender 1–2 min, until completely smooth. With a countertop blender, fill it no more than halfway, take out the center cap of the lid, cover the hole with a folded towel and blend in batches. Hot soup can blow a sealed lid off.

Return the soup to the pot over low heat. Stir in the cream or coconut milk and warm 2–3 min without letting it boil. Taste and add salt. If it's too thick, thin with broth or water a few Tbsp at a time.
Ladle into bowls and top each with about 2 tsp pepitas.
tips: For deeper flavor, roast the squash first: toss the cubes with the oil and roast at 425°F for 25–30 min, until browned at the edges. Then simmer with the broth just 10 min.
Pre-cut squash skips the hardest step. You need about 2 lb (6 cups) of cubes.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze up to 3 months, ideally before adding the cream. Reheat in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring, until steaming. Add the pepitas when you serve.

recipes.title: Caesar Salad

items: 2 large heads romaine (about 1½ lb), chopped into 1-inch pieces, washed and dried
½ cup shaved or grated parmesan (1½ oz)
1 clove garlic, finely grated or minced
1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts (2 small), each halved horizontally into thin cutlets
¼ cup vegetable oil, for frying

steps: Make the dressing: whisk the mayo, parmesan, lemon juice, Dijon, Worcestershire, garlic, anchovy paste and pepper in a small bowl. Whisk in water 1 tsp at a time until it pours. Chill until serving.

Pat the chicken cutlets dry and season both sides with the salt. Put the flour, egg and panko in 3 shallow dishes. Coat each cutlet in flour, dip it in egg, then press it into the panko on both sides.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until a panko crumb sizzles right away. Cook the cutlets 3–4 min per side, until deep golden and they read 165°F in the thickest part. Turn the heat to medium if the crumbs brown too fast.
Drain the chicken on paper towels and rest 5 min, then slice into strips.
In a large bowl, toss the romaine with about ⅔ of the dressing until every leaf is coated. Add more dressing to taste.
Divide among plates and top with the croutons, parmesan and sliced chicken.
tips: Bacon instead of chicken: cook 6 slices bacon in the skillet over medium heat 8–12 min, until crisp. Drain, crumble and scatter over the salad.
Dry the romaine well in a salad spinner or with towels. Wet leaves water down the dressing and it slides off.
recipes.storage: Dressed salad doesn't keep, so toss only what you'll eat. Dressing keeps 4 days in the fridge and the chicken 3 days. Re-crisp the chicken at 400°F in the oven or air fryer for 5–8 min, until it reads 165°F.

recipes.title: Chia Pudding

items: 1 cup milk (dairy or any plant milk)
½ cup fresh blueberries or raspberries

steps: For the chocolate version, start by whisking the cocoa and extra maple syrup with 2–3 Tbsp of the milk in a medium bowl until smooth. This keeps the cocoa from clumping.
Add the rest of the milk, the maple syrup and vanilla to the bowl and whisk. Add the chia seeds and whisk 30 sec.
Let it sit 10 min, until it starts to thicken.
Whisk again, breaking up any clumps at the bottom. Divide between 2 jars, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hr or overnight, until thick and spoonable.
Stir before serving and add a splash of milk if it's too thick. Top with berries and pepitas.
tips: The second whisk is the key step. Skip it and the seeds settle into a solid clump at the bottom.
Too thin after chilling? Stir in 1 Tbsp more chia and chill 30 min more.
Make 4 or 5 jars at once for grab-and-go breakfasts through the week.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 5 days in covered jars. Add the fruit and pepitas just before eating so the seeds stay crunchy. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry

items: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
3 cups broccoli florets (from 1 medium head), bite-size
2 medium carrots, peeled and sliced ¼ inch thick on an angle
1 cup frozen shelled edamame or peas

steps: Whisk the sauce ingredients in a small bowl until the cornstarch dissolves. Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the chicken in one layer and cook 5–7 min, turning once it's browned, until no pink remains and it reads 165°F. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil, the broccoli and carrots. Stir-fry 2 min, until the broccoli turns bright green.
Add 2 Tbsp water and cover the pan. Steam 2 min, until the carrots are crisp-tender. Uncover, add the edamame or peas and stir-fry 1 min more.
Return the chicken and any juices. Whisk the sauce again, since the cornstarch settles, and pour it in.
Stir 1–2 min, until the sauce bubbles, thickens and coats everything in a glossy layer.
Serve over rice and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
tips: Cut the vegetables to a similar size so they cook evenly.
Thighs stay juicier than breast and are harder to overcook.
Add a pinch of red pepper flakes or 1 tsp sriracha to the sauce for heat.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or in the microwave, until hot (165°F). Freezes up to 2 months, though the broccoli softens.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan
equipment: Rimmed sheet pan with a wire rack

items: 2 large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ lb), halved horizontally into 4 cutlets about ½ inch thick
1 large egg, beaten with 1 Tbsp water
½ cup vegetable oil, for frying
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)

steps: Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Set a wire rack in a rimmed sheet pan. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.
Pat the cutlets dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper. Set up 3 shallow dishes: the flour, the beaten egg, and the breadcrumbs mixed with ¼ cup parmesan.
Coat each cutlet in flour and shake off the extra, dip it in egg and let it drip, then press it into the breadcrumbs on both sides.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until a pinch of breadcrumbs sizzles right away. Fry 2 cutlets at a time 3–4 min per side, until deep golden and they read 165°F in the thickest part. Move them to the wire rack.
While the chicken fries, cook the spaghetti until al dente. Drain and toss with 2 cups of the warm marinara.
Spoon about ¼ cup of the remaining marinara over each cutlet and top with the mozzarella. Broil 2–4 min, until the cheese is melted and browned in spots. Watch closely.
Serve the chicken over the spaghetti, sprinkled with parmesan.
tips: Air fryer: spray the breaded cutlets with oil and cook at 400°F for 10–12 min, flipping halfway, until 165°F. Add the sauce and cheese and cook 1–2 min more to melt.
Let the breaded cutlets sit 10 min before frying so the coating sticks better.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the cutlets on a sheet pan in a 375°F oven 12–15 min, until they reach 165°F; the microwave makes the breading soggy. Freeze breaded, uncooked cutlets up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge before frying.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie Soup with Biscuits
equipment: 5- to 6-quart Dutch oven or soup pot

items: Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Heat the oven to the temperature on the biscuit package (usually 350°F) with a rack in the middle. Set the biscuits 2 inches apart on a baking sheet.
Melt the butter in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6–8 min, stirring often, until the onion is soft and see-through. Stir in the garlic for 30 sec.
Put the biscuits in the oven and bake as the package says, usually 13–17 min, until deep golden brown.
While they bake, sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly 1 min, until no dry flour shows.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, so no lumps form. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then lower to medium-low and simmer 10 min, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the chicken, peas and thyme. Simmer 3–5 min, until the chicken is hot and the peas are bright green. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and set a warm biscuit on top of each.
tips: Keep it at a gentle simmer once the milk is in. A hard boil can make it separate.
No rotisserie chicken? Simmer 1 lb boneless chicken breast in the broth 15–20 min, until it reads 165°F, then shred it and use the broth in the soup.
For a heartier soup, add 1 diced Yukon Gold potato with the carrots and simmer until fork-tender.
recipes.storage: Soup keeps in the fridge up to 4 days. It thickens as it sits, so reheat it on the stove over medium-low heat with a splash of broth or milk. Freezing isn't recommended; the milk can turn grainy. Keep biscuits in a sealed bag at room temperature up to 2 days and rewarm them in a 350°F oven for 5 min.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.cook: 6 hr on low or 3–4 hr on high, plus 15 min
recipes.total: 6 hr 30 min on low (3 hr 30 min–4 hr 30 min on high)
equipment: Medium saucepan with lid (for the rice)

items: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, cut into 1½-inch chunks
¾ cup heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk
6 cups cooked basmati rice (from 2 cups uncooked)

steps: Add the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, tomato sauce, tomato paste, garam masala, cumin, paprika and salt to a 6-quart slow cooker. Stir until the tomato paste is mixed in and the chicken is coated.
Cover and cook on low 6 hr or on high 3–4 hr, until the chicken is tender and reads 165°F in the thickest piece.
About 30 min before serving, cook the rice in a medium saucepan as the package directs.
Stir the cream into the slow cooker. If it was on low, switch to high. Cover and cook 15 min more, until hot and slightly thickened.
Taste and add salt if needed. If the sauce looks thin, cook uncovered on high 10–15 min more.
Warm the naan in a dry skillet over medium heat about 1 min per side. Spoon the curry over rice, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with the naan.
tips: Add the cream only at the end. Hours of cooking can make it separate.
For deeper flavor, cook the onion in 1 Tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat 6–8 min, until golden, before it goes in.
Chicken breast works too. Cook it 4 hr on low or 2–2½ hr on high so it doesn't dry out.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months (the sauce can look grainy after freezing; stir well as it heats). Reheat on the stove over medium-low heat or in the microwave until it reaches 165°F. Store rice separately and refrigerate it within 2 hr.

recipes.title: Chili with Cornbread

items: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) black or pinto beans, rinsed and drained
½ cup water or beef broth
1 box (8.5 oz) cornbread mix, such as Jiffy
1 tsp butter or cooking spray, for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Grease an 8×8-inch baking dish.

Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef and onion and cook 8–10 min, breaking up the meat, until the beef is browned with no pink (160°F) and the onion is soft. Spoon off most of the fat.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and salt and stir 1 min, until fragrant.

Stir in the tomatoes, beans and ½ cup water. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered 30 min, stirring every 5–10 min so the bottom doesn't stick, until thick. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.

While the chili simmers, stir the cornbread mix, egg and milk in a bowl until just combined. A few lumps are fine. Spread in the dish and bake 15–20 min, until golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 min and cut into 9 squares.
Taste the chili and add more salt if it needs it. Ladle into bowls. Top with avocado, sour cream in lines and cilantro. Serve with the cornbread.
tips: Start with 2 Tbsp chili powder. Taste after 15 min of simmering and add the last 1 Tbsp if you want more heat.
Slow cooker: brown the beef and onion first, then cook everything (except the cornbread) on low 6–8 hr.
Other cornbread mixes call for different amounts of egg, milk and oil. Follow your box.
recipes.storage: Chili keeps in the fridge up to 4 days or the freezer up to 3 months. Reheat on the stove over medium heat, stirring, until steaming (165°F). Cornbread keeps 2 days wrapped at room temperature. Warm it in the microwave 10–15 sec.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Rolls
equipment: Stand mixer with dough hook, or a large bowl
Unflavored dental floss or a serrated knife

items: 2¼ tsp (1 packet) instant or active dry yeast
⅓ cup unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
3½ cups all-purpose flour (about 440 g), spooned and leveled, plus more as needed
1 Tbsp butter, softened, for the bowl and pan
⅓ cup unsalted butter, very soft
¾ cup packed light brown sugar

steps: In the stand mixer bowl, stir together the warm milk, yeast and 1 tsp of the sugar. If using active dry yeast, let it stand 5–10 min, until foamy. Milk hotter than 115°F can kill the yeast.
Add the rest of the sugar, the egg and the melted butter and stir. Add the flour and salt and mix on low with the dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.

Knead on medium-low 6–8 min, or 8–10 min by hand on a lightly floured counter, until smooth, stretchy and slightly tacky but not sticking to a clean finger. If it's very sticky, add flour 1 Tbsp at a time.
Shape the dough into a ball and put it in a lightly buttered bowl. Cover and let it rise in a warm spot (75–80°F) 1–1½ hr, until doubled. A floured finger pressed in should leave a dent that stays.

Butter the 9×13-inch pan. On a lightly floured counter, press out the air and roll the dough into a 16×12-inch rectangle with a long side facing you. Spread the soft butter to the edges. Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle it evenly over the butter, leaving a ½-inch bare strip along the far long edge.

Roll the dough up tightly from the long side closest to you and pinch the seam closed. Cut into 12 rolls about 1⅓ inches wide with floss or a serrated knife. Set them cut side up in the pan in 3 rows of 4.
Cover and let the rolls rise 30–45 min, until puffy and touching. During the last 20 min, heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle.
Bake 22–25 min, until golden brown and the center roll reads 190°F. If the tops brown too fast, cover loosely with foil. Cool in the pan 10 min.
Beat the cream cheese and butter with a hand mixer until smooth, about 1 min. Beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until fluffy. Spread over the warm (not hot) rolls.
tips: Overnight: after cutting the rolls and setting them in the pan, cover tightly and refrigerate up to 16 hr. In the morning, let them sit at room temperature 45–60 min, until puffy, then bake.
To cut with floss, slide it under the log, cross the ends over the top and pull. It cuts cleanly without squashing the swirl.
Too much flour makes dry rolls. Spoon the flour into the cup and level it instead of scooping, or weigh it.
recipes.storage: Iced rolls keep in the fridge, covered, up to 4 days because of the cream cheese icing. Freeze baked rolls without icing up to 2 months. Reheat a roll in the microwave 15–20 seconds, or a pan of rolls covered in foil at 300°F for 10–15 min.

recipes.title: Corn Chowder
equipment: 12-inch deep skillet or sauté pan (at least 4 quarts)

items: 2 Tbsp unsalted butter (use if skipping the bacon)
1 tsp dried thyme (or 1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves)
2 medium Yukon Gold potatoes (about 1 lb), peeled and cut into ½-inch dice
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
3 cups corn kernels (fresh from 4 ears, or frozen)

steps: If using bacon, cook it in the skillet over medium heat 6–8 min, stirring, until crisp. Move it to a paper-towel-lined plate and leave about 2 Tbsp drippings in the pan. If skipping bacon, melt the butter over medium heat instead.
Add the onion and celery and cook 6–8 min, stirring, until soft and translucent. Sprinkle in the flour and thyme and stir 1 min, until the flour coats the vegetables and smells toasty.
Slowly pour in the broth while whisking so no lumps form, then whisk in the milk. Add the potatoes, salt and pepper.

Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often. Reduce to medium-low and simmer uncovered 15–18 min, stirring every few min so the bottom doesn't scorch, until the potatoes are tender when pierced. Don't let it boil hard or the milk can separate.
Stir in the corn and simmer 5 min, until the corn is hot and tender.
Press about a quarter of the potatoes against the side of the pan with a potato masher and stir. The chowder thickens in 1–2 min. Taste and add salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with the crumbled bacon if you made it.
tips: Frozen corn goes in straight from the bag. Add 1–2 min to the corn step.
For a richer chowder, swap 1 cup of the milk for half-and-half.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. It doesn't freeze well; the potatoes turn grainy and the milk can separate. Reheat gently over medium-low heat, stirring, with a splash of milk if it's thick.

recipes.title: Cowboy Caviar

items: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, rinsed and drained
1½ cups corn kernels (frozen and thawed, or canned and drained)
¾ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

steps: Rinse the beans and chickpeas in a colander under cold water. Let them drain well, about 5 min. Extra water dilutes the dressing.
Quarter the tomatoes. Dice the pepper and onion into pieces about the size of a bean. Chop the cilantro.
In a small bowl, whisk the oil, vinegar, lime juice, sugar, chili powder and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Put everything in a large bowl, pour on the dressing and toss gently until coated.
Cover and chill at least 30 min so the flavors soak in. Stir, taste and add more salt or lime if needed. Serve with tortilla chips.
tips: If raw onion tastes too sharp to you, soak the diced onion in cold water 10 min, then drain.
Making it a day ahead? Stir in the tomatoes and cilantro just before serving so they stay fresh.
Spoon leftovers over grilled chicken or into tacos for an easy dinner.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days in a sealed container. It gets juicier as it sits, so stir before serving. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken and Spinach Pasta

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into ¾-inch pieces

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the rigatoni until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Meanwhile, pat the chicken dry and season with ½ tsp salt and the pepper. Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the chicken in a single layer and cook 5–7 min, turning once or twice, until golden and it reads 165°F in the thickest piece.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and cook 30 sec, until fragrant. Pour in the cream, scraping up the browned bits, then stir in the parmesan. Simmer 2–3 min, until slightly thickened.
Add the spinach a handful at a time, stirring until it wilts, about 1 min.
Add the rigatoni and ¼ cup pasta water and toss until glossy and coated. Add more pasta water if it looks tight.
Taste for salt and serve sprinkled with parsley.
tips: Don't crowd the chicken. If it won't fit in one layer, brown it in two batches so it sears instead of steaming.
Boneless thighs work too and stay juicier. Cook them to 165°F the same way.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium-low heat with a splash of milk or water until the chicken reaches 165°F. Don't freeze; the cream sauce separates.

recipes.title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken

items: 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ lb total), sliced in half horizontally to make 4 thin cutlets
2 Tbsp olive oil (or oil from the sun-dried tomato jar)
⅓ cup oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped
12 oz pasta, cooked, or 1 loaf crusty bread, sliced

steps: Pat the cutlets dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the cutlets 3–4 min per side, until golden and they read 165°F in the thickest part. Work in 2 batches if they don't fit with space between them. Move them to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to the same pan and cook 1 min, stirring, until fragrant.
Pour in the cream, add the Italian seasoning and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer gently 3 min, until it thickens slightly.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the parmesan until melted. Add the spinach and stir 1–2 min, until wilted.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Spoon the sauce over it and warm 1–2 min. Serve over pasta, or with bread for the sauce.
tips: If the cutlets are uneven, pound the thick end to ½ inch so they cook evenly.
Add the parmesan over low heat. If the cream boils hard after the cheese goes in, the sauce can turn grainy.
Boneless chicken thighs work too. Cook them 5–6 min per side, to 165°F.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a covered skillet over low heat with a splash of milk or broth until the chicken is hot (165°F). Don't freeze; the cream sauce separates.

recipes.title: Creamy Vodka Rigatoni

items: 2 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat and add the 2 Tbsp salt.
Add the rigatoni and cook 1 min less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water before you drain it.
While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add the shallot and garlic and cook 2–3 min, stirring, until soft and fragrant but not browned.
Add the tomato paste and cook about 4 min, stirring often, until it darkens to brick-red and starts to stick to the pan.
Pour in the vodka, if using, and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble about 1 min, until it no longer smells sharp.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the cream and chili flakes and simmer gently 1–2 min, until the sauce is smooth and pale orange.

Add the drained pasta, ¼ cup pasta water and the parmesan. Toss over low heat 1–2 min, adding more pasta water a splash at a time, until the sauce is glossy and clings to the pasta. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve topped with basil and more parmesan.
tips: Skipping the vodka is fine. Use 2 Tbsp pasta water instead.
Keep the heat low once the parmesan goes in. Over high heat it clumps and the sauce turns grainy.
For protein, stir in browned Italian sausage or sliced cooked chicken at the end.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days in a sealed container. Reheat in a skillet over low heat with a splash of milk or water, stirring until creamy. Don't freeze; the cream sauce turns grainy.

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Wings

items: 2 lb chicken wings, split into flats and drumettes, tips removed
1 Tbsp aluminum-free baking powder (not baking soda)
½ cup cayenne pepper hot sauce, such as Frank's RedHot
½ cup ranch or blue cheese dressing
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch sticks

steps: Pat the wings very dry with paper towels. Any moisture left on the skin keeps it from crisping.
In a large bowl, mix the baking powder, salt and garlic powder. Add the wings and toss until each one has a thin, even dusting.
Arrange the wings in the air fryer basket in a single layer, not touching. Most baskets fit about 1 lb, so cook in 2 batches if needed.

Air fry at 380°F for 20 min. Flip the wings, raise the heat to 400°F and cook 5–8 min more, until deep golden and crisp and the thickest drumette reads at least 165°F. Wings are juiciest at 175–185°F.
While the wings cook, whisk the melted butter and hot sauce together in a large bowl.
For buffalo wings, toss the hot wings in the sauce right before serving. Serve with the dressing, celery and carrots.
tips: Oven method: line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set a wire rack on it. Spread the coated wings on the rack and bake at 425°F on the middle rack for 45–50 min, flipping halfway, until crisp and 165°F.
Use aluminum-free baking powder; regular can taste metallic. Never swap in baking soda, which tastes soapy.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in the air fryer at 375°F for 5–7 min, until hot (165°F) and crisp again. Sauced wings soften as they sit, so sauce only what you'll eat.

recipes.title: Crispy Pork Carnitas
recipes.cook: 8–10 hr on low or 5–6 hr on high, plus 5 min under the broiler
recipes.total: 8 hr 30 min–10 hr 30 min on low (5 hr 30 min–6 hr 30 min on high)

items: 3–4 lb boneless pork shoulder (pork butt), thick fat trimmed, cut into 3-inch chunks
1 medium yellow onion, sliced ½ inch thick
16 small corn or flour tortillas, warmed
½ small white onion, finely diced

steps: Mix the salt, cumin, oregano and chili powder in a small bowl. Rub it all over the pork chunks.
Spread the sliced onion and garlic in the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker and set the pork on top. Squeeze the orange and lime juice over the pork, then tuck the squeezed halves in around it.
Cover and cook on low 8–10 hr or on high 5–6 hr, until the pork falls apart when pressed with a fork. It will be well past the safe 145°F, around 195–205°F, which is what lets it shred.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Lift the pork onto a cutting board, throw away the citrus halves and shred the meat with two forks, pulling out any fatty bits.
Spread the pork in a single layer on a rimmed sheet pan and spoon ½ cup of the cooking juices over it.
Broil 3–5 min, until the edges are brown and crisp. Watch closely after 3 min. Stir and broil 2 min more if you want extra crispy bits.
Serve in warm tortillas with diced onion, cilantro, salsa and lime wedges.
tips: Use two sheet pans if the pork is piled up. Crowded meat steams instead of crisping.
Skim the fat off the leftover juices and save them. Spoon a little over leftovers before reheating so they stay juicy.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freezer up to 3 months, with some of the juices. Reheat in a hot skillet over medium-high heat 3–5 min, until sizzling and crisp at the edges.

recipes.title: Egg Fried Rice

items: 3 cups cooked white rice, chilled overnight

steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your hands so the grains are separate. Beat the eggs with the salt.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the eggs and scramble 1–2 min, until set with no runny parts. Move to a plate and chop into small pieces.
Raise the heat to medium-high and add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil. Add the garlic and peas and stir 1 min, until the garlic smells fragrant.

Add the rice and spread it in an even layer. Let it sit 1–2 min without stirring so the bottom toasts, then stir and spread it out again. Repeat for 5–6 min total, until the rice is hot and some grains are crisp.
Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil around the edge of the pan and toss to coat.
Stir in the eggs and most of the scallions and cook 1 min more, until heated through. Top with the rest of the scallions.
tips: Use cold, cooked rice. Fresh rice turns mushy. If yours is fresh, spread it on a sheet pan and refrigerate uncovered 1 hr first.
Add diced cooked chicken, ham or shrimp with the rice for a full meal.
recipes.storage: Cool within 2 hr and refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat, or in the microwave with 1 Tbsp water, covered, until steaming hot (165°F). Reheat only once.

recipes.title: Egg Muffins

items: 1 cup cooked sausage crumbles or diced ham

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Coat a 12-cup muffin tin well with cooking spray, including the top rim.
Divide the bell pepper, sausage or ham and cheese evenly among the cups, about ¼ cup in each.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until no streaks of white remain. Pour into a liquid measuring cup.
Pour the eggs over the fillings until each cup is about ¾ full. They puff as they bake.
Bake 20–25 min, until puffed, the tops are set and don't jiggle, and the center of one reads 160°F.
Cool in the tin 5 min. They sink a little as they cool. Run a butter knife around each one and lift it out.
tips: Always use cooked sausage or ham. Raw meat won't cook through in the time it takes the eggs to set.
Sauté the bell pepper 3–4 min first if you like it soft instead of crisp.
Silicone muffin cups, or paper liners sprayed with oil, make them release more easily.
recipes.storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months in a zip-top bag. Reheat in the microwave 30–45 sec from the fridge, or 60–90 sec from frozen, until hot in the center.

recipes.title: Egg Salad Toast

items: 2 Tbsp fresh chives or dill, finely chopped
4 slices sourdough or whole-grain bread, toasted
1 Tbsp fresh chives or dill, chopped

steps: Fill a medium saucepan with enough water to cover the eggs by 1 inch and bring it to a boil over high heat. Fill a large bowl with the ice and cold water.
Lower the eggs in gently with a slotted spoon. Turn the heat to medium so the water keeps a steady, gentle boil, and cook 11–12 min.
Move the eggs to the ice bath and leave them 10 min, until cold. This stops the cooking and makes them easier to peel.
Tap each egg all over, peel under running water and pat dry. Chop into ½-inch pieces so the salad stays chunky.
In a medium bowl, stir the mayo, mustard, 2 Tbsp herbs, salt and pepper. Gently fold in the eggs.
Pile onto the toast and sprinkle with the rest of the herbs.
tips: Eggs that are a week or more old peel more easily than very fresh ones.
A gray-green ring around the yolk means the eggs overcooked. Stick to 12 min and chill them right away.
Add a squeeze of lemon or 1 Tbsp pickle relish for more tang.
recipes.storage: Egg salad keeps in the fridge up to 3 days. Unpeeled hard-boiled eggs keep up to 1 week. Toast the bread just before serving. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Fettuccine Alfredo

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
1 cup finely grated parmesan (about 3 oz), plus 2 Tbsp to serve
½ tsp black pepper, plus more to serve
1 lb large shrimp, peeled, deveined and patted dry
or 2 cups broccoli florets, cut bite-size

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.

If using shrimp, melt 1 Tbsp of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp in a single layer, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and cook 1–1½ min per side, until pink and opaque all the way through. Move to a plate.
Cook the fettuccine until al dente. If using broccoli, add it to the pot for the last 3 min. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, melt the remaining butter (3 Tbsp, or all 4 Tbsp if you skipped the shrimp) in the skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 30 sec, until fragrant. Pour in the cream and simmer gently 3 min, until slightly thickened.
Take the skillet off the heat. Stir in the parmesan a handful at a time until smooth. Adding it off the heat keeps it from turning grainy.
Add the pasta, the shrimp or broccoli, the pepper and ¼ cup pasta water. Toss with tongs until the sauce coats every strand, adding more pasta water if it's thick. Taste for salt.
Serve right away with more parmesan and black pepper.
tips: Grate the parmesan yourself. Pre-shredded cheese has anti-caking powder that makes the sauce clumpy.
The sauce thickens fast as it cools. Serve on warm plates and loosen it with a splash of pasta water if needed.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Fridge up to 3 days (2 days with shrimp). Reheat in a skillet over low heat with a splash of milk, stirring, until hot; the microwave can make it oily. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Freezer Breakfast Burritos

items: 3 cups frozen tater tots or shredded hash browns
1 lb bulk breakfast sausage (or 1 lb bacon, cooked crisp and crumbled)
½ cup thick salsa, drained of extra liquid

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Spread the tots on the sheet pan and bake 20–25 min (or as the package says), turning once, until crisp. Chop them roughly.

Meanwhile, cook the sausage in the skillet over medium-high heat 8–10 min, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned with no pink left and it reads 160°F. Drain on paper towels and wipe out the skillet.
Whisk the eggs with the salt and pepper. Melt the butter in the skillet over medium-low heat, add the eggs and stir slowly 3–4 min, until set with no runny egg left.
Spread the eggs, sausage and tots on plates or the sheet pan and cool 15–20 min, until they stop steaming. Warm filling makes steam, which makes soggy tortillas and ice crystals.
Wrap the tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave 20–30 sec, so they fold without cracking.
Down the center of each tortilla, layer eggs, sausage, tots, ¼ cup cheese and 1 Tbsp salsa. Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom. Wrap each burrito in foil.
Put the wrapped burritos in freezer bags, press out the air, label with the date and freeze.
tips: To reheat from frozen, remove the foil, wrap the burrito in a damp paper towel and microwave 1 min per side, then 30–60 sec more, until hot in the center (165°F). For a crisp outside, finish it in a dry skillet over medium heat 1–2 min per side.
Use thick salsa or drain it well, so the tortillas don't get soggy.
Don't let the cooked filling sit out more than 2 hr before freezing.
recipes.storage: Freezer up to 3 months, or fridge up to 4 days. Reheat from frozen in the microwave (see tips), or bake still in foil at 375°F for 30–35 min, until hot in the center (165°F).

recipes.title: Fried Eggs on Avocado Toast

items: 2 thick slices sourdough, or 2 English muffins, split
1 tsp everything bagel seasoning, or hot sauce to taste

steps: Toast the bread or English muffins until golden and crisp.
Halve and pit the avocado. Scoop it into a small bowl and mash with a fork. Stir in the lemon juice and salt.
Melt the butter in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat until it foams. Crack in the eggs, leaving space between them.

Cook 2–3 min, until the whites are fully set and no longer clear, the edges are lightly crisp and the yolks are still runny. If the whites near the yolk are slow to set, cover the pan for the last 30 sec.
Spread the avocado on the toast. Slide an egg onto each piece with a thin spatula.
Finish with black pepper and everything seasoning or hot sauce. Eat right away.
tips: Crack each egg into a small cup first, then slide it into the pan. It keeps the yolk whole and the shell out.
For over-easy eggs, flip them and cook 20–30 sec more.
recipes.storage: Does not keep. The toast goes soggy and the avocado browns, so make it just before eating.

recipes.title: Frosted Pumpkin Bars

items: 1 can (15 oz) pumpkin purée (not pumpkin pie filling)
2 cups all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
¼ cup (½ stick) unsalted butter, softened

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Coat the 10×15-inch pan well with nonstick spray.
In a large bowl, whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil and sugar until smooth.

In a second bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. Add it to the pumpkin mixture and stir with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain. Overmixing makes the bars tough.
Spread the batter evenly into the pan, pushing it into the corners. Bake 25–30 min, until the center springs back when pressed lightly and a toothpick comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, at least 1½ hr. Frosting melts on warm bars.

Make the frosting: beat the cream cheese and butter with a hand mixer on medium 1–2 min, until smooth. Add the powdered sugar 1 cup at a time on low, then the vanilla, and beat on medium 1 min, until fluffy.
Spread the frosting over the cooled bars. Warm the caramel in the microwave 10–15 seconds, until pourable, and drizzle it over the top in thin lines with a spoon.
Chill 30 min to set, then cut into 24 squares (4 rows by 6).
tips: For a warmer spice flavor, swap the cinnamon for 1 Tbsp pumpkin pie spice.
Make ahead: bake and frost the day before, cover and refrigerate. Add the caramel just before serving so the lines stay neat.
A 9×13-inch pan works too. The bars are thicker, so bake 30–35 min.
recipes.storage: Fridge, covered, up to 5 days; the cream cheese frosting must stay cold. Freeze frosted bars without the caramel up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge. Serve cold or after 15 min at room temperature.

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Shrimp Orzo
equipment: 12-inch deep skillet or wide pot with lid

items: 1 lb large shrimp (21–25 per lb), peeled and deveined, patted dry
2½ cups low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
2 large handfuls baby spinach (about 2 oz), or ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley

steps: Toss the shrimp with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add the orzo and toast 2–3 min, stirring, until lightly golden. Add the garlic and stir 30 sec, until fragrant.

Pour in the broth and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn to medium-low and simmer uncovered about 8 min, stirring every minute or two so it doesn't stick, until the orzo is almost tender and most of the broth is absorbed.
If the pan looks dry, add ¼ cup broth. Nestle the shrimp into the orzo in one layer, cover and cook 3–4 min, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, parmesan and spinach until the spinach wilts and the orzo is creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
tips: Thaw frozen shrimp overnight in the fridge, or in a bowl of cold water for 10–15 min.
Shrimp are done when they curl into a loose C. A tight O means they're overcooked.
Orzo keeps soaking up liquid. Stir in a splash of broth right before serving if it gets thick.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over low heat with a splash of broth, or in the microwave at 50% power, stirring. Doesn't freeze well; the shrimp turn rubbery.

recipes.title: Garlic Shrimp and Mushrooms with Ravioli

items: 2 packages (9 oz each) fresh cheese ravioli
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
8 oz cremini or white mushrooms, sliced ¼ inch thick
1 lb large shrimp, peeled, deveined and patted dry

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Season the shrimp with ½ tsp salt and the pepper.
Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer with no fat and cook 6–8 min, stirring only once or twice, until they release their liquid and turn golden brown.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and, once it melts, the shrimp in a single layer. Cook 1–1½ min per side, until pink and opaque. Stir in the garlic for the last 30 sec.
Meanwhile, cook the ravioli as the package says, usually 3–5 min, until they float and are tender. Save ½ cup of the cooking water and lift the ravioli out with a slotted spoon so they don't tear.
Add the ravioli to the skillet with the lemon juice and 2–3 Tbsp of the cooking water. Toss gently until glossy.
Sprinkle with parsley, taste for salt and serve.
tips: The dry pan is on purpose. Mushrooms soak up butter added at the start and steam instead of browning.
Shrimp go from done to rubbery in about 1 min. Pull them as soon as they curl into a loose C shape.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Fridge up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat with a splash of water just until warm; overheating toughens the shrimp. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Glazed Salmon over Rice

items: 2 salmon fillets (6 oz each, about 1 inch thick), skin on or off
8 oz asparagus, woody ends snapped off, or 8 oz green beans, trimmed

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Start the rice now if it isn't already cooked.

Toss the asparagus or green beans with the olive oil and ¼ tsp salt on a rimmed sheet pan and spread in one layer. Roast asparagus 10–12 min or green beans 15–20 min, until tender and browned in spots.
While the vegetables roast, whisk the soy sauce, honey, sriracha and garlic in a small bowl. Pat the salmon dry and season with ¼ tsp salt.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the salmon, flesh-side down, and sear 3–4 min without moving, until golden and it releases easily.
Flip the salmon and turn the heat down to medium-low. Pour in the glaze. Honey burns quickly, so keep it at a gentle bubble.
Cook 3–4 min more, spooning the glaze over the fish, until the glaze is thick and sticky and the salmon reads 145°F in the thickest part or flakes easily with a fork.
Serve the salmon over rice with the vegetables. Spoon over any glaze left in the pan and sprinkle with scallions.
tips: If the glaze gets too thick before the fish is done, stir in 1 Tbsp water.
Cooking for 4? Double everything and sear the salmon in 2 batches, or use 2 skillets.
Air fryer: brush the salmon with half the glaze and air fry at 400°F for 8–10 min, to 145°F. Simmer the rest of the glaze 1–2 min in a small pan and spoon it over.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat gently in the microwave at 50% power 1–2 min, or eat it cold over rice. Cool cooked rice within 2 hr.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Pineapple Rice
equipment: Heavy-bottomed 3-quart saucepan with a tight lid

items: 1½ cups long-grain white or jasmine rice
1 (20-oz) can pineapple tidbits or chunks in juice
Water, as needed to make 2¼ cups liquid with the pineapple juice
½ red bell pepper, finely diced, optional
¼ cup toasted macadamia nuts or toasted coconut flakes, optional

steps: Drain the pineapple through a strainer set over a liquid measuring cup, saving the juice. Add water to the juice to make 2¼ cups. Set the pineapple aside.
Rinse the rice in the strainer under cold water, swishing with your hand, until the water runs mostly clear. Shake off as much water as you can.
Melt the butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat. Add the rice and stir 2 min, until it smells nutty and the edges of the grains look a little translucent.
Add the juice mixture, soy sauce, salt and the bell pepper, if using. Stir once and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly and cook 18 min. Don't lift the lid or stir.
Take the pot off the heat and let it sit, still covered, 5 min.
Fluff with a fork. Gently fold in the pineapple and most of the green onions, then top with the rest of the onions and the nuts or coconut.
tips: Keep the heat truly low. The juice has natural sugar, so the bottom can scorch. If it does, don't scrape the scorched layer into the rest.
Make it a meal by folding in 1 cup diced ham or cooked chicken with the pineapple. It's great with teriyaki London broil, honey garlic chicken thighs or sticky pork ribs.
Still crunchy? Sprinkle 2–3 Tbsp water over the top, cover and cook on low 5 min more. Too sweet? Use 1 cup juice and 1¼ cups water next time.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hr of cooking; keeps up to 4 days sealed. Freezer up to 2 months, flattened in a zip-top bag. Reheat covered in the microwave with 1–2 Tbsp water sprinkled over, until steaming. Day-old pineapple rice makes good fried rice.

recipes.title: Herb-Crusted Pork Tenderloin

items: 1 pork tenderloin (1–1¼ lb), silver skin trimmed
2 medium yellow squash, cut into ½-inch half-moons

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle.

On a rimmed sheet pan, toss the green beans and squash with the oil, salt and pepper and spread them in a single layer. Roast 20–25 min, stirring once, until tender and browned in spots. They go in first because they take longer than the pork.
While the vegetables roast, pat the pork dry. Mix the Dijon, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper and rub it all over the pork.

Heat the oil in the oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the pork 5–6 min total, turning every 1–2 min, until browned on all sides. Let each side release on its own before turning so the crust stays on.
Move the skillet to the oven next to the vegetables. Roast 12–18 min, until the pork reads 145°F in the thickest part.
Move the pork to a cutting board and rest 5 min. Put an oven mitt over the skillet handle; it stays hot for a long time.
Slice the pork ½ inch thick and serve with the vegetables. A little pink in the center is safe at 145°F.
tips: For a thicker crust, press 3 Tbsp panko mixed with 1 Tbsp chopped fresh parsley onto the mustard rub before searing.
Tenderloin is lean and dries out fast past 150°F. Start checking at 12 min.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat slices covered in a skillet over low heat with a splash of broth, or eat cold. Reheat the vegetables in the microwave 1–2 min.

recipes.title: Hibachi Fried Rice with Yum Yum Sauce

items: 4 cups cooked white rice, chilled at least 12 hr (from about 1⅓ cups uncooked)
1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into ¾-inch pieces, or 1 lb peeled deveined shrimp
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Whisk the sauce ingredients together, adding water until it pours like heavy cream. Chill while you cook.
Break up the cold rice with your hands so there are no clumps.

Heat the oil and 1 Tbsp butter in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add the protein, season with salt, pepper and 1 Tbsp soy sauce and cook until the chicken reads 165°F (5–7 min) or the shrimp are pink and opaque (2–3 min). Move it to a plate.
Add 1 Tbsp butter, the onion and the peas and carrots. Cook 3–4 min, stirring, until the onion softens.
Add the rice, the remaining 2 Tbsp butter, the garlic and 2 Tbsp soy sauce. Spread it out and cook 4–5 min, turning it every minute, until hot and starting to crisp.
Push the rice to one side. Pour the eggs into the empty spot and scramble about 1 min, until set, then stir them into the rice.
Return the protein and its juices and toss 1 min to heat through. Serve with the yum yum sauce drizzled over the top in lines.
tips: Use rice cooked the day before and chilled. Fresh rice turns mushy. In a pinch, spread fresh rice on a sheet pan and refrigerate 30 min uncovered.
If your pan is small, cook the rice in 2 batches. A crowded pan steams the rice instead of frying it.
The sauce tastes better after an hour in the fridge, so make it first or the day before.
recipes.storage: Cool leftover fried rice within 2 hr and refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or microwave covered until steaming hot (165°F). The sauce keeps 1 week in the fridge.

recipes.title: Homemade Pepperoni Pizza

items: 1 lb pizza dough, at room temperature
2 Tbsp all-purpose flour or cornmeal, for the peel
1 tsp olive oil, for the crust

steps: Set a pizza stone or steel on a rack in the upper third of the oven and heat to 500°F for 45 min. Take the dough out of the fridge at the same time so it warms up and stretches easily.

Sprinkle the peel with the flour or cornmeal. On a floured counter, press the dough into a disk, then stretch it over your knuckles into a 12-inch round, leaving the edge a little thicker. Lay it on the peel.
Spread the sauce thinly, leaving a 1-inch border. Scatter the mozzarella, then the pepperoni and jalapeño, if using. Brush the border with the oil.
Shake the peel gently to make sure the pizza slides. If it sticks, lift the edge and toss a little more flour underneath.
Slide the pizza onto the hot stone with a quick forward-and-back jerk. Bake 7–10 min, until the crust has dark spots and the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots.
Pull it out with the peel, rest 2 min so the cheese sets, then slice.
tips: Garlic flatbread slices: stretch a second 1 lb dough ball, brush it with 2 Tbsp olive oil mixed with 2 cloves grated garlic, top with 1 cup mozzarella and bake 6–8 min the same way. Cut into strips.
No peel? Build the pizza on parchment on an upside-down sheet pan and slide it, parchment and all, onto the stone.
If the dough keeps shrinking back as you stretch it, cover it 10 min to relax, then try again.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days, wrapped. Reheat slices in a covered skillet over medium heat 3–5 min, until the bottom is crisp and the cheese melts, or in a 400°F oven 5–7 min.

recipes.title: Honey-Garlic Pork Tenderloin with Green Beans

items: 1 pork tenderloin (about 1¼ lb), silver skin trimmed, patted dry
¼ tsp kosher salt (for the green beans)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan with foil, since the glaze gets sticky.

Simmer the honey, soy sauce, garlic and butter in the saucepan over medium heat 2 min, stirring, until slightly thickened. Pour half into a small bowl and set it aside for serving. Keep the other half for brushing.

Season the pork with the salt and pepper and set it in the middle of the pan. Toss the green beans with the oil and ¼ tsp salt and spread them around the pork in one layer. Brush the pork with some of the brushing glaze.
Roast 20–25 min, brushing the pork with the rest of the brushing glaze halfway through, until the thickest part reads 145°F and the green beans are tender and browned in spots.
Move the pork to a cutting board and rest 5 min. Rewarm the serving glaze if it has thickened.
Slice the pork ½ inch thick. Serve with the green beans and spoon the serving glaze over the top.
tips: Keep the serving glaze away from the brush you use on the raw pork, so it's safe to pour over the cooked meat.
If the beans brown before the pork is done, move them to a plate and keep roasting the pork.
A little pink in the center is normal and safe at 145°F after the rest.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat sliced pork and beans in a covered skillet over medium-low heat with 1 Tbsp water, or in the microwave at 50% power, so the pork doesn't dry out. Cooked pork freezes up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Imitation Crab Pasta

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
8 oz imitation crab, pulled into bite-size strips
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the pasta until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook 1 min, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the crab and cook 2 min, stirring gently, just until warm. It's already cooked, so it only needs heating.

For the pesto version, take the pan off the heat and stir in the pesto; cooking pesto turns it dull and oily. For the cream version, pour in the cream, simmer 2 min, then take it off the heat and stir in the parmesan until smooth.
Add the pasta and ¼ cup pasta water and toss until coated. Add more water if it looks dry.
Squeeze in the juice of half the lemon, season with salt and pepper and toss. Cut the other half into wedges to serve.
tips: Imitation crab is made from cooked fish, so long cooking makes it rubbery. Add it near the end.
Add 1 cup frozen peas to the pasta pot for the last 2 min for color.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a skillet over low heat with a splash of water or milk. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Italian Pasta Salad

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
½ cup sliced black olives, drained
1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 red bell pepper, cut into ½-inch dice
¼ cup torn fresh basil leaves

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the rotini for the full package time, until tender. Cold pasta firms up, so don't undercook it.
Drain and rinse under cold water, tossing, until cool. Shake the colander well; leftover water dilutes the dressing.
If making the homemade dressing, shake the oil, vinegar, oregano, salt and pepper in a jar until blended.
In a large bowl, combine the pasta, mozzarella, tomatoes, olives, chickpeas and bell pepper. Pour ½ cup of the dressing over and toss well.
Cover and chill at least 30 min so the flavors blend.
Right before serving, toss in the basil and the remaining ¼ cup dressing, since the pasta soaks up the first round. Taste and add salt if needed.
tips: Add the basil at the end. It turns black if it sits in dressing overnight.
Add 4 oz diced salami for a meat version.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days in a sealed container. Don't leave it out more than 2 hr. Stir in a splash of dressing or olive oil before serving leftovers. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: John's Award-Winning Chili

items: 2 lb sirloin tips (2 packages), cut into ½-inch cubes
2 cans (28 oz each) whole peeled tomatoes, broken up by hand or with a knife
½ cup amber ale (about ⅓ of a 12-oz bottle)
1 to 2 cans (15 oz each) kidney beans, rinsed well and drained

steps: Heat the oil in a 7-quart Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Brown the sirloin cubes in 2 or 3 batches so they don't crowd, 5 to 7 min per batch, until deeply browned on all sides. Move each batch to a bowl with a slotted spoon.
Add the ground sirloin to the same pot over medium-high heat. Break it up with a spoon and cook 6 to 8 min, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Return the browned sirloin cubes to the pot. Spoon off any excess grease, leaving about 1 tbsp.

Add the onions, jalapeño if using, garlic, bell peppers and poblanos. Stir in the chili powder, cumin, oregano and cayenne. Cook over medium heat, stirring often, about 7 min, until the vegetables soften and the spices smell toasty.
Stir in the tomatoes, ale, broth, brown sugar and beans. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Lower the heat to medium-low so the chili simmers gently. Cook partly covered for 1½ to 2 hr, stirring often so it doesn't stick, until the beef cubes are tender and the chili is thick.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.
tips: John usually doubles the recipe, triples the meat and doubles the chili powder and cumin.
Skip the jalapeño for a milder pot, or use 4 or more cans of mixed beans like pinto, black and kidney.
Chili tastes even better the next day, so it's a good make-ahead dish.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring and adding a splash of broth if thick, until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Korean Ground Beef Bowls

items: 1 Tbsp butter or neutral oil (for the eggs)

steps: Bring the rice and 2 cups water to a boil in the saucepan over high heat. Cover, turn to low and cook 15 min. Rest off the heat, covered, 10 min.

Meanwhile, cook the beef in the 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat 6–8 min, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left and it reads 160°F. Tilt the pan and spoon off most of the fat, leaving about 1 Tbsp.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Stir in the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and gochujang, if using. Simmer 2–3 min, stirring, until the sauce reduces and the beef looks glossy.
Stir the mayo and sriracha together for the drizzle.

Heat the butter in the nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and cook 3–4 min, until the whites are fully set and the edges are crisp. Cover for the last minute if the tops of the whites are still clear.
Spoon rice into bowls and top with beef, cucumber, scallions and sesame seeds. Add a fried egg and drizzle the sriracha mayo in lines.
tips: Use 90% lean beef or ground turkey for less grease. Cook turkey to 165°F.
Double the sauce if you like extra to soak into the rice.
