Quick-pickle the cucumber: toss it with 1 Tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt while the beef cooks.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the beef and rice stored apart from the cucumber. Cool the rice within 2 hr. Reheat the beef and rice covered in the microwave 1–2 min, until steaming. The beef freezes up to 3 months. Fry the eggs fresh.

recipes.title: Lemon Blueberry Baked Oats

items: 1 tsp butter or nonstick spray, for the dish
1 cup fresh or frozen blueberries (don't thaw frozen ones)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle. Grease the baking dish.
Mash the banana in the bowl with a fork until mostly smooth. Whisk in the eggs, milk, yogurt, maple syrup and lemon zest until combined.
Stir in the oats, baking powder and salt. Fold in the blueberries, then spread the mixture evenly in the dish.
Bake 25–30 min, until the top is golden, the edges pull away from the dish and the center is set and doesn't jiggle (160°F in the middle).
Cool 10 min before cutting into 4 squares, so it firms up.
tips: Use old-fashioned rolled oats. Quick oats turn pasty and steel-cut oats won't soften in time.
For a glaze, whisk ½ cup powdered sugar with 1 Tbsp lemon juice and drizzle it over the cooled oats.
Bake it on Sunday and reheat a square each morning.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 5 days, covered. Freeze squares wrapped individually up to 3 months. Reheat in the microwave 45–60 sec, or 1½–2 min from frozen.

recipes.title: Lemon Icebox Pie

items: 8 oz cream cheese, softened at room temperature about 1 hr
½ cup fresh lemon juice (from 3–4 lemons)
1 Tbsp finely grated lemon zest (from 2 lemons)
1½ cups graham cracker crumbs (about 11 full sheets)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle.

Make the crust: stir the graham cracker crumbs, sugar, salt and melted butter in a bowl until it looks like wet sand. Press it firmly into the bottom and up the sides of the 9-inch glass pie plate with a flat-bottomed measuring cup.
Bake the crust 8–10 min, until fragrant and slightly darker at the edges. Cool completely on a wire rack, about 30 min. A warm crust softens the filling.
Beat the cream cheese with a hand mixer on medium about 2 min, until completely smooth with no lumps. Any lumps now stay in the finished pie.
On low speed, beat in the condensed milk until smooth, scraping the bowl. Add the lemon juice and zest and beat 1 min. The lemon juice thickens the mixture as you beat.
Pour the filling into the cooled crust and smooth the top. Cover loosely and refrigerate at least 4 hr, or overnight, until firm enough to slice cleanly.
Top with a lemon round in the center, or one on each slice. Cut with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry.
tips: A store-bought 9-inch graham cracker crust works. Skip the crust steps and start with the filling.
Use fresh lemons, not bottled juice. Bottled juice tastes flat and the pie may not set as firmly.
Make it the day before. It slices more cleanly after chilling overnight.
recipes.storage: Fridge, covered, up to 4 days. Don't leave it out more than 2 hr. Freeze up to 1 month wrapped tightly and thaw in the fridge about 4 hr. Serve cold.

recipes.title: Lettuce Wraps

items: 1 lb ground pork or ground chicken
1 can (8 oz) water chestnuts, drained and diced
1 head butter lettuce (about 12 leaves), leaves separated

steps: Stir the hoisin, soy sauce, rice vinegar and sriracha in a small bowl. Separate the lettuce leaves, rinse and pat dry.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the meat and cook 6–8 min, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned with no pink left. Pork should read 160°F and chicken 165°F. Spoon off extra fat if using pork.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir 30–60 sec, until fragrant.
Add the water chestnuts and sauce. Cook 2 min, stirring, until the sauce coats the meat and looks glossy.
Spoon about ⅓ cup filling into each lettuce cup and top with scallions.
tips: Dry the lettuce well or the cups get watery.
Add 1 cup diced mushrooms or a diced bell pepper with the meat for more vegetables.
Serve any extra filling over rice.
recipes.storage: Filling keeps in the fridge up to 4 days or the freezer up to 3 months. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat or in the microwave until hot (165°F). Store the lettuce separately, wrapped in a damp paper towel, up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Loaded Baked Potatoes

items: 4 medium russet potatoes (8–10 oz each), scrubbed and dried
4 Tbsp unsalted butter, cut into 4 pats

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil.
Prick each potato 6–8 times with a fork. Rub with the oil, sprinkle with the salt and set them on the pan.
Bake 50–60 min, until the skins are crisp and a fork slides into the center with no resistance. If you have a thermometer, the center reads 205–210°F.
While the potatoes bake, lay the bacon in a cold 12-inch skillet. Cook over medium heat 8–12 min, turning a few times, until crisp. Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate, then crumble.
Cut a slit along the top of each potato and squeeze the ends toward the middle to open it. Fluff the inside with a fork and tuck in a pat of butter and a pinch of pepper.
Top each potato with ¼ cup cheddar so it melts on the hot potato, then the bacon, a spoonful of sour cream and the scallions.
tips: Twice-baked: after baking, let the potatoes cool 10 min. Cut off the top third, scoop the insides into a bowl leaving a ¼-inch shell, and mash with the butter, the sour cream and ¾ cup of the cheddar. Refill the shells, top with the rest of the cheese and bake at 425°F for 15–20 min, until golden on top. Finish with bacon and scallions.
Don't wrap the potatoes in foil. Foil traps steam and gives you soft, damp skins.
To cook the bacon in the oven instead, lay it on a second foil-lined pan and bake it next to the potatoes for the last 15–20 min.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the toppings stored separately. Reheat potatoes at 375°F for 15–20 min or in the microwave 2–3 min, then add the cold toppings. Twice-baked potatoes freeze up to 3 months; bake from frozen at 375°F for 40–50 min, until 165°F in the center.

recipes.title: Loaded Sweet Potatoes with Chipotle Black Beans

items: 4 medium sweet potatoes (about 8 oz each), scrubbed
1 (15 oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup frozen or canned corn (drained if canned)
1 tsp adobo sauce from the can

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan with foil, since the potatoes leak sticky syrup.
Prick each sweet potato 4–5 times with a fork, rub with the oil and sprinkle with salt. Bake 45–60 min, until a knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.
About 10 min before the potatoes are done, combine the beans, corn, chipotle, adobo sauce and 2 Tbsp water in the saucepan. Warm over medium heat about 5 min, stirring, until hot. Season with salt.
Stir the sour cream, lime juice and a pinch of salt together. Add water 1 tsp at a time until it drizzles off a spoon.
Slit each potato lengthwise, push the ends toward the middle to open it and fluff the inside with a fork. Season with a pinch of salt.
Spoon the beans into the potatoes. Drizzle the lime sour cream in lines, then top with cotija, scallions and avocado. Serve with lime wedges.
tips: Short on time: microwave the pricked potatoes 8–10 min, turning once, until soft, then roast at 425°F for 10 min to crisp the skins.
Chipotles vary in heat. Start with half a pepper and taste before adding the rest.
Freeze the leftover chipotles flat in a zip-top bag so you can break off one at a time.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the potatoes and beans stored apart from the sour cream and avocado. Reheat the potatoes and beans in the microwave 2–3 min, or at 350°F for 15 min, then add the cold toppings.

recipes.title: Marinated Steak Tips
equipment: Gallon zip-top bag or large bowl

items: 2 lb sirloin steak tips (flap meat), cut into 1½-inch chunks
1 tsp neutral oil, for the griddle
½ tsp kosher salt, for finishing

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, Worcestershire, olive oil, brown sugar, Dijon, vinegar, garlic, pepper and onion powder in a bowl or zip-top bag. Don't add salt yet; the soy carries plenty.
Add the steak tips, press out the air and refrigerate 4–8 hr. Don't go past 12 hr, or the outside turns mushy.
Take the meat out 30–40 min before cooking. Discard the marinade, set the pieces on a rack or paper towels and pat them dry. Wet meat steams instead of searing.
Heat a griddle or cast-iron skillet over high heat 10 min, with a cooler zone if you can. It's ready when a drop of water skitters and vanishes. Wipe on a thin film of oil.

Lay the pieces down with space between them and don't touch them for 2–3 min. Turn to sear the other sides, about 2 min more, moving pieces to the cooler zone as they finish. Pull them at 125°F for medium-rare.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 5–8 min; the temperature climbs about 5°F. Season with the kosher salt and slice against the grain if the pieces are large.
tips: Doneness, pull temp then final temp after resting: rare 115°F to 120°F, medium-rare 125°F to 130°F, medium 135°F to 140°F, medium-well 145°F to 150°F.
Ask for flap meat or sirloin tips, not stew beef. Flap meat is tender enough to sear but turns to leather if overcooked.
No griddle? Broil on the top rack on high 3–4 min per side, or use cast iron in batches so the pan stays hot.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Leftovers are best sliced cold for sandwiches, since reheating pushes them past medium. If you reheat, do it briefly in a hot skillet.

recipes.title: Mexican Rice, Refried Beans and Guacamole
equipment: 2- to 3-quart saucepan with a tight lid

items: ½ medium yellow onion, finely diced
½ cup tomato sauce (from an 8-oz can)

steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the rice and cook 4–5 min, stirring often, until most of the grains turn light golden and smell toasty.
Add the onion and garlic and stir 2 min, until the onion starts to soften.
Stir in the tomato sauce, broth, cumin and salt. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer 18–20 min without lifting the lid, until the liquid is absorbed.
Take the pan off the heat and rest 5 min, still covered. Fluff with a fork.
While the rice cooks, warm the refried beans with 3 Tbsp water in a small saucepan over medium-low heat 5 min, stirring often, until smooth and hot.
For the guacamole, scoop the avocados into a bowl and mash with a fork, leaving it chunky. Stir in the lime juice, cilantro and salt. Taste and add more salt or lime if needed.
Serve the rice, beans and guacamole side by side on each plate.
tips: Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear, then shake it dry before toasting. It cooks up fluffier.
Don't lift the lid while the rice simmers. The trapped steam is what cooks it.
Use vegetable broth to keep the whole plate meatless.
recipes.storage: Rice and beans keep in the fridge up to 4 days. Cool the rice within 2 hr of cooking. Reheat the rice in the microwave with 1 Tbsp water, covered, until steaming. Reheat the beans in a pan over medium-low heat with a splash of water. Guacamole browns fast. Press plastic wrap onto its surface and eat it by the next day.

recipes.title: Misir Wot (Ethiopian Red Lentils)
equipment: Medium heavy pot or Dutch oven

items: 1 cup red lentils, rinsed until the water runs mostly clear
2 medium red or yellow onions, finely chopped
1 Tbsp grated fresh ginger (about a 1-inch piece)
3 cups water, plus more as needed
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
4 injera from an Ethiopian market, or 4 flatbreads

steps: Put the onions in the dry pot over medium heat. Cook 8–10 min, stirring often, until soft and jammy. If they stick or start to brown, add 1 Tbsp water.
Add the butter, garlic, ginger, berbere and tomato paste. Cook 2 min, stirring constantly, until fragrant and deep red. Don't let the spices scorch.
Add the lentils, 3 cups water and the salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn it down to low so it simmers gently.

Simmer uncovered 20–25 min, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the lentils break down and the stew is thick like oatmeal. If it gets too thick before the lentils are soft, add water ¼ cup at a time.
Taste and add salt. Serve warm with injera or flatbread for scooping.
tips: Berbere blends vary a lot in heat. Start with 2 Tbsp. You can stir in more at the end and simmer 2 min.
For a flavor closer to the restaurant, use niter kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter) in place of the butter.
It thickens as it sits. Stir in a splash of water when reheating.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 5 days or freezer up to 3 months. Reheat in a pot over medium-low heat with a splash of water, stirring, or in the microwave 2–3 min, stirring halfway.

recipes.title: Miso-Glazed Salmon

items: 4 salmon fillets (about 6 oz each, 1 inch thick), skin on or off
1 tsp neutral oil or nonstick spray, for the foil

steps: Set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler and turn the broiler to high. Line the sheet pan with foil and grease it lightly.
Whisk the miso, honey, soy sauce and vinegar until smooth.
Pat the salmon dry and set it on the foil, skin side down, 1 inch apart. Brush the tops and sides with half the glaze.
Broil 4 min, then brush on the rest of the glaze.

Broil 3–6 min more, until the top is caramelized and the thickest part flakes easily and reads 145°F. Watch closely. If the glaze starts to blacken before the fish is done, cover it loosely with foil.
Serve over rice with cucumber, scallions and sesame seeds.
tips: Thinner fillets (about ¾ inch) cook in about 6 min total, so start checking early.
For deeper flavor, coat the salmon in the glaze and marinate it in the fridge up to 2 hr.
Air fryer: cook at 400°F for 8–10 min, brushing with glaze halfway, until it reads 145°F.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Eat it cold over rice, or reheat gently in the microwave at 50% power 1–2 min, or at 275°F for 15 min. Freezing dries it out.

recipes.title: Orange Chicken
equipment: Wire rack on a sheet pan, or a paper towel-lined plate

items: 1½ lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 cups neutral oil (enough for ¼ inch in a 12-inch skillet)
½ cup fresh orange juice (from 1–2 oranges)

steps: Whisk all the sauce ingredients in a small saucepan until the cornstarch dissolves. Set it aside, off the heat.
Season the chicken with the salt and toss it in the beaten egg. Put the cornstarch in a shallow bowl and toss the chicken in it a few pieces at a time, shaking off the extra.
Heat ¼ inch of oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches about 350°F, or a pinch of cornstarch sizzles right away.
Fry the chicken in 2 batches without crowding, 3–4 min per side, until golden and crisp and the center reads 165°F. Move to the rack or paper towels.
While the second batch fries, whisk the sauce again and bring it to a simmer over medium heat, whisking. Cook 1–2 min, until thick and glossy.
Put the chicken in a large bowl, pour the sauce over and toss until coated. Serve right away over rice with scallions.
tips: Air fryer: spray the coated chicken with oil and air fry at 400°F for 12–15 min, shaking halfway, until it reads 165°F.
Toss the chicken with the sauce right before serving. It loses its crunch if it sits.
Keep the oil at a steady sizzle. If it smokes, lower the heat. If the chicken sits quietly, raise it.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. The coating softens. Reheat in an air fryer at 375°F for 5–6 min or in a 400°F oven for 8–10 min, until hot (165°F).

recipes.title: Pad See Ew

items: 12 oz fresh wide rice noodles (or 6 oz dried wide rice noodles, soaked as the package says)
8 oz boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast, sliced ¼ inch thick
3 cups broccoli florets in bite-size pieces, or 1 bunch Chinese broccoli (stems cut into 1-inch pieces, leaves kept separate)

steps: Separate the noodles into single strands. If they're stiff from the fridge, microwave them 30–60 sec, until they pull apart without tearing.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy, sugar and 1 Tbsp water in the small bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in the wok over high heat until it shimmers. Add the chicken in one layer and cook 2 min without moving it. Add the garlic and stir-fry 1–2 min more, until the chicken is no longer pink and reads 165°F.
Add the broccoli (stems first if using Chinese broccoli) and 2 Tbsp water. Stir-fry 2 min, until bright green and crisp-tender. Add any Chinese broccoli leaves for the last 30 sec.
Push everything to one side. Add 1 Tbsp oil to the empty side, crack in the eggs and scramble 30–60 sec, until just set.

Add the last 1 Tbsp oil, the noodles and the sauce. Toss gently to coat. Then spread them out and let them sit undisturbed 30 sec at a time, tossing between, for 2–3 min total, until they have charred spots.
Toss everything together and serve right away.
tips: Don't double it in one pan. Cook 2 batches, or the noodles steam and break instead of charring.
No dark soy sauce? Use 1 extra tsp soy sauce plus 1 tsp molasses or brown sugar.
Try a pinch of chili flakes and a splash of rice vinegar at the table, the way Thai restaurants serve it.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Rice noodles harden when cold, so reheat in a skillet over medium heat with 1–2 Tbsp water, covered for 1 min, or microwave covered with a damp paper towel. Doesn't freeze well.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Gnocchi with Chicken and Pesto

items: 1 large boneless skinless chicken breast (about 10 oz), cut into ¾-inch pieces

steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the chicken 5–7 min, turning once or twice, until golden and it reads 165°F in the thickest piece. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil. Break apart any gnocchi stuck together and add them straight from the package in a single layer. No boiling needed.
Cook 4–5 min without stirring, until the bottoms are golden. Toss and cook 3–4 min more, until golden on most sides and soft inside when you bite one.
Turn off the heat. Return the chicken and any juices, add the pesto and toss to coat.
Top with parmesan and fresh basil and serve.
tips: If the gnocchi are still chewy inside, add 2 Tbsp water, cover 1–2 min to steam, then uncover and let them crisp again.
Add 1 cup halved cherry tomatoes with the pesto for color.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; the gnocchi lose their crisp edges in the fridge. Leftovers keep up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat 4–5 min, until the chicken reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Pappardelle with Meat Sauce

items: 1 medium carrot, peeled and finely chopped
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
1 oz parmesan, shaved with a peeler (about ½ cup)
¼ cup fresh basil leaves, torn

steps: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and carrot and cook 8–10 min, breaking up the meat, until browned with no pink left (160°F) and the vegetables are soft.
Spoon off extra fat. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 min, until the paste darkens slightly.
Add the tomatoes, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat to low, partly cover and simmer at least 30 min, stirring now and then, until thick.
About 15 min before the sauce is done, bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the pappardelle until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Stir the milk into the sauce and simmer 2 min. Taste and add salt if needed.
Add the pappardelle and a splash of pasta water to the sauce and toss gently with tongs until coated.
Top with shaved parmesan and basil.
tips: For a richer sauce, simmer it up to 1½ hr on low. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Use half ground beef and half ground pork for a softer, richer sauce; cook it to 160°F the same way.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze the sauce alone up to 3 months. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water until it reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Pasta Marinara with Garlic Toast

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
8 slices Italian bread, ¾ inch thick
¼ cup torn fresh basil leaves

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.
Meanwhile, warm the oil and sliced garlic in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat 1–2 min, until the garlic sizzles and smells fragrant but hasn't browned.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, pepper flakes, ½ tsp salt and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat and simmer 15 min, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.
Cook the pasta until al dente, about 1 min less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.

Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Mix the butter and garlic powder, spread it on the bread and sprinkle with the parmesan. Broil on a rimmed sheet pan 2–3 min, until golden at the edges. Watch closely; it burns fast.
Add the pasta and ¼ cup pasta water to the sauce and toss over medium heat 1–2 min, until the sauce clings. Add more pasta water if it looks dry.
Serve topped with parmesan and basil, with the garlic toast on the side.
tips: If the sauce tastes sharp, add another pinch of sugar.
Double the sauce and freeze half for a fast weeknight dinner.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze the sauce alone up to 3 months. Reheat pasta in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water. Garlic toast is best fresh; rewarm it in a 350°F oven 3–4 min.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Cinnamon Rolls
equipment: Stand mixer with dough hook, or a large bowl

items: ½ cup whole milk, warmed to 105–110°F
1 cup canned pumpkin purée (not pumpkin pie filling)
¼ cup unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
4 cups all-purpose flour, plus up to ¼ cup more for kneading
1 Tbsp softened butter, for the bowl and pan
⅓ cup unsalted butter, very soft

steps: Stir the yeast and 1 tsp of the brown sugar into the warm milk. It should feel warm, not hot (105–110°F). Wait 5–10 min, until foamy. If it doesn't foam, the yeast is dead; start over with fresh yeast.

Add the rest of the brown sugar, the pumpkin, egg, melted butter, salt, pumpkin pie spice and 3½ cups of the flour. Mix on low with the dough hook (or a wooden spoon) until a shaggy dough forms, then add the last ½ cup flour.
Knead on medium-low 6–8 min (8–10 min by hand), until smooth and springy. It stays a little sticky. Add more flour 1 Tbsp at a time only if it sticks to everything.
Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover and let it rise in a warm spot 1–1½ hr, until doubled.

Grease a 9×13-inch pan. Roll the dough on a lightly floured counter into a 16×12-inch rectangle. Spread the soft butter over it, leaving a ½-inch bare strip along one long edge. Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle it evenly over the butter.

Roll up tightly from the long side opposite the bare strip and pinch the seam closed. Cut into 12 rolls about 1⅓ inches wide. Set them cut side up in the pan, cover and let rise 45 min, until puffy and touching. Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle during the last 20 min.
Bake 22–26 min, until golden brown and the center roll reads 190°F. Cover loosely with foil after 15 min if the tops brown too fast.
Beat the cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar and maple syrup until smooth. Let the rolls cool 10 min, then spread the icing over them while still warm.
tips: Overnight option: after shaping, cover and refrigerate up to 16 hr. Let them sit at room temperature 45–60 min before baking.
Cut the log with unflavored dental floss. Slide it under, cross the ends and pull; it won't squash the rolls.
If the pumpkin looks watery, blot it with paper towels first, or the dough will need a lot more flour.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, covered, because of the cream cheese icing. Freeze un-iced baked rolls up to 2 months. Rewarm in the microwave 15–20 sec, or covered in a 300°F oven 10 min.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Pie Chia Pudding
equipment: Medium bowl or 1-quart jar with lid

items: 1 cup milk (dairy or unsweetened plant milk)
⅓ cup canned pumpkin purée (not pumpkin pie filling)
1 Tbsp maple syrup, plus more to taste

steps: Whisk the milk, pumpkin, maple syrup, spice, vanilla and salt in the bowl until smooth, with no orange streaks.
Whisk in the chia seeds. Let it sit 10 min, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hr, or overnight, until thick and spoonable.
Toast the pepitas in the dry skillet over medium heat 3–4 min, shaking the pan, until they puff and start to pop. Let them cool.
Stir the pudding, taste and add more maple syrup if you like. Divide between 2 jars and top each with 2 Tbsp yogurt and 1 Tbsp pepitas.
tips: Too thick in the morning? Stir in 1–2 Tbsp milk. Too thin? Stir in 1 tsp chia and wait 15 min.
No pumpkin pie spice: use ¼ tsp cinnamon, ⅛ tsp ground ginger and a pinch each of nutmeg and cloves.
Freeze the rest of the can of pumpkin in ⅓-cup portions for next time.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, covered. Add the yogurt and pepitas just before eating so the pepitas stay crunchy. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Quesadillas
equipment: Rimmed sheet pan (to keep them warm)

items: 1½ cups shredded cooked chicken, or 1 can (16 oz) refried beans

steps: Heat the oven to 200°F and put a rimmed sheet pan inside. It keeps finished quesadillas warm while you cook the rest.
Warm the chicken or beans in the microwave 1 min, so the middle heats through in the pan.
Lay the tortillas flat. Spread or scatter a quarter of the chicken or beans over one half of each tortilla. Top with ½ cup cheese and fold the bare half over.
Melt about 1½ tsp butter in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 or 2 quesadillas.

Cook 2–3 min, until the bottom is golden brown. Flip with a wide spatula and cook 2–3 min more, until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted. If the outside browns before the cheese melts, lower the heat a little.
Move to the sheet pan in the oven. Repeat with the rest, adding butter for each one.
Rest 1 min, then cut each into 3 wedges. Serve with sour cream and salsa on the side.
tips: Leftover taco meat, black beans or sautéed peppers and onions all work as fillings.
For a crowd, bake them. Brush the outsides with melted butter and bake on a sheet pan at 425°F for 10–12 min, flipping once.
recipes.storage: Best fresh. Leftovers keep in the fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a dry skillet over medium-low heat 3–4 min per side, or in an air fryer at 350°F for 4–5 min, until hot and crisp.

recipes.title: Ramen Noodle Stir-Fry

items: 2 packs (3 oz each) instant ramen, seasoning packets discarded, or 6 oz flat rice noodles
1 boneless skinless chicken breast (about 8 oz), sliced into thin bite-size strips
2 Tbsp neutral oil, plus 1 tsp for the noodles
1 medium carrot, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Stir the sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Cook the ramen 2 min, just until the noodles separate. For rice noodles, cook 1–2 min less than the package says. Drain, rinse briefly with cold water and toss with 1 tsp oil so they don't stick.

Season the chicken with the salt. Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the chicken 4–5 min, stirring now and then, until browned and it reads 165°F. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil, the broccoli and carrot and stir-fry 2 min. Add the bell pepper and 2 Tbsp water and stir-fry 2 min more, until the water is gone and the vegetables are crisp-tender.
Turn the heat to high. Add the noodles, chicken and sauce and toss with tongs 1–2 min, until the noodles are hot and evenly coated.
tips: Rice noodles break easily. Cook them only until just bendable, since they soften more in the pan.
Shrimp or tofu work in place of chicken. Cook shrimp 1–2 min per side, until pink and opaque.
Add chili crisp or sriracha at the table for heat.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or in the microwave, until hot (165°F). The noodles soften as they sit.

recipes.title: Salmon Poke Bowl
equipment: Medium saucepan with a tight lid (or a rice cooker)

items: 8–10 oz sushi-grade salmon, skin removed, kept cold

steps: Buy salmon sold as sushi-grade or for raw eating, from a fish counter you trust. Keep it in the fridge until the moment you cut it.

Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water, swishing it with your hand, until the water runs mostly clear, about 1 min. Put it in a saucepan with 1¼ cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 min. Turn off the heat and rest 10 min, still covered.
Stir 1 Tbsp rice vinegar, the sugar and salt until dissolved. Gently fold it into the warm rice and let it cool to just warm, about 10 min.
While the rice rests, cut the salmon into ¾-inch cubes with a sharp knife. In a medium bowl, toss it with the soy sauce, sesame oil and 1 tsp rice vinegar. Cover and refrigerate 10–30 min.
Slice the cucumber, avocado and scallions.
Divide the rice between 2 bowls. Arrange the salmon, cucumber and avocado on top and sprinkle with scallions.
Spoon on the chili crisp and drizzle the Japanese mayo in lines. Eat right away.
tips: Put the salmon in the freezer for 15 min before cutting. It firms up and cubes cleanly.
Can't find sushi-grade fish? Use cooked salmon or cooked shrimp instead of raw.
Short on time? Use plain warm white rice with a splash of rice vinegar.
recipes.storage: Raw fish does not keep. Eat poke the day you make it, and keep the cut salmon cold until you serve it. Leftover plain rice keeps 4 days in the fridge if cooled within 2 hr.

recipes.title: Salmon Sushi Bake
equipment: 8×8-inch metal or ceramic baking dish (not glass, since it goes under the broiler)

items: 1½ cups sushi rice (short-grain), rinsed until the water runs clear
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
¼ cup Japanese mayo (such as Kewpie)
3 packs roasted seaweed snack sheets (about 30 sheets)

steps: Combine the rinsed rice and 1¾ cups water in the saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 15 min. Take it off the heat and let it steam, still covered, 10 min.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Stir the rice vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Set the salmon on a foil-lined sheet pan, rub it with the oil and season lightly with salt and pepper. Bake 12–15 min, until it flakes easily and reads 145°F in the thickest part. Leave the oven on.

Pour the vinegar mixture over the hot rice and fold it in with a spatula, cutting through rather than stirring so the grains stay whole. Press the rice evenly into the baking dish and sprinkle with the furikake.
Flake the salmon with a fork. Mix it with the cream cheese, ¼ cup mayo and sriracha to taste until evenly combined.
Spread the salmon mixture over the rice in an even layer. Bake 10 min, until hot all the way through.
Switch the oven to broil on high and broil 2–3 min, until the top browns in spots. Watch closely, since mayo burns fast.
Stir the 3 Tbsp mayo and 1 Tbsp sriracha together and drizzle over the top in lines. Scatter with scallions. Scoop onto seaweed sheets and add a slice of avocado and cucumber to each bite.
tips: Make it ahead: spread the salmon mixture over the rice (step 6) but don't bake it. Cover and chill up to 1 day, then bake 20 min at 400°F and broil.
Leftover cooked salmon works here. Skip step 3 and use about 2 cups flaked salmon.
No Kewpie? Use regular mayo with 1 tsp rice vinegar stirred in.
recipes.storage: Best the day it's made. Fridge up to 2 days, covered, with the avocado and cucumber kept separate. Reheat at 350°F for 10–15 min or in the microwave 1–2 min. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Salsa Verde Shredded Chicken
recipes.cook: 6 hr on low or 3–4 hr on high
recipes.total: 6 hr 15 min on low (3 hr 15 min–4 hr 15 min on high)

items: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs or breasts, fully thawed
12 small corn or flour tortillas, warmed, or 4 cups cooked rice

steps: Make sure the chicken is fully thawed. Frozen chicken sits too long at unsafe temperatures in a slow cooker.
Lay the chicken in an even layer in a 6-quart slow cooker. Sprinkle with the cumin, garlic powder and salt, then pour the salsa verde over the top.
Cover and cook on low 6 hr or on high 3–4 hr, until the chicken is very tender and reads 165°F in the thickest piece. Keep the lid on; each peek adds about 15 min.
Shred the chicken with two forks right in the pot. It should pull apart easily. If it resists, cover and cook 30 min more.
Stir in the lime juice and cilantro and let it sit 5 min so the meat soaks up the sauce. Taste and add salt if needed.
Serve over rice or in warm tortillas with avocado and sour cream. Use a slotted spoon for tacos so they don't get soggy.
tips: Chicken breasts dry out faster than thighs. Check them at 4 hr on low or 2½ hr on high.
For crispy edges, spread the shredded chicken on a sheet pan and broil 3–4 min about 6 inches from the heat.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days with some of the sauce. Freezer up to 3 months in freezer bags; thaw overnight in the fridge. Reheat covered in the microwave or in a skillet over medium heat until it reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Sausage and Pepper Pasta

items: 12 oz short pasta, such as penne or rigatoni
1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
1 lb Italian sausage, casings removed (or links sliced ½ inch thick)
2 red bell peppers, sliced ¼ inch thick
1 medium yellow onion, sliced ¼ inch thick
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook 6–8 min, breaking it up (or turning the slices), until browned with no pink left (160°F). Move it to a plate and leave the fat in the pan.
Add the peppers and onion with a pinch of salt. Cook 8–10 min, stirring only every couple of minutes, until soft and charred in spots.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta until al dente. Save 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Add the garlic to the vegetables and cook 1 min, until fragrant. Return the sausage to the pan.
Add the pasta, parmesan and ½ cup pasta water and toss over medium heat 1–2 min, until glossy. Season with salt and pepper and serve.
tips: Cheesy skillet version: at the end, lower the heat to medium-low, stir in the cream, then the cheddar a handful at a time until melted and creamy. Use less pasta water and sprinkle the parmesan on top.
In a hurry? Swap in 1 jar (12 oz) roasted red peppers, drained and sliced, and add them with the garlic.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or in the microwave, until it reaches 165°F. The cheesy version reheats best on the stove with a splash of milk.

recipes.title: Sausage Baked Ziti

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
1 lb bulk Italian sausage (or links with casings removed)
¼ cup torn fresh basil leaves

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt.
Cook the ziti 2 min less than the package says so it stays firm while it bakes. Drain.

Meanwhile, cook the sausage and onion in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat 8–10 min, breaking up the sausage, until browned with no pink left (160°F). Spoon off extra fat. Stir in the garlic for 30 sec, then the marinara, and simmer 5 min.
In a bowl, stir together the ricotta, egg and ¼ cup parmesan.
Toss the ziti with the sausage sauce. Spread half in a 9×13-inch baking dish, dot with spoonfuls of the ricotta mixture, then cover with the rest of the pasta.
Sprinkle the mozzarella and the remaining ¼ cup parmesan over the top. Cover tightly with foil, tented so it doesn't touch the cheese.
Bake covered 20 min. Uncover and bake 15–20 min more, until the sauce bubbles at the edges and the cheese is melted and spotted brown.
Rest 10 min so it sets and scoops cleanly. Scatter the basil over the top and serve.
tips: Make ahead: assemble, cover and refrigerate up to 24 hr. Bake covered 30 min, then uncovered 20 min, until the center reads 165°F.
Undercooking the pasta matters. Fully cooked ziti turns mushy after 35 min in the oven.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months, wrapped well. Reheat portions in the microwave, or the covered dish in a 350°F oven 20–30 min, until the center reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Sausage, White Bean and Kale Soup
recipes.cook: 6–8 hr on low or 3–4 hr on high, plus 30 min
recipes.total: 6 hr 50 min–8 hr 50 min on low (3 hr 50 min–4 hr 50 min on high)

items: 1 lb bulk Italian sausage (or links with casings removed)
2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) diced tomatoes, with their juice
1 bunch curly kale (about 8 oz), stems removed, leaves chopped
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
6 slices crusty bread, ¾ inch thick

steps: Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook 6–8 min, breaking it into small pieces, until browned with no pink left (160°F). Spoon off the extra fat.
Move the sausage to a 6-quart slow cooker. Add the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, beans, tomatoes, broth, Italian seasoning and parmesan rind, if using. Stir.
Cover and cook on low 6–8 hr or on high 3–4 hr, until the carrots are tender.
Stir in the kale. If it was on low, switch to high. Cover and cook 20–30 min, until the kale is tender and dark green.
Fish out the parmesan rind. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. The sausage is salty, so taste before adding any.
For the garlic toast, heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat. Mix the butter and garlic powder, spread it on the bread and broil on a rimmed sheet pan 2–3 min, until golden at the edges.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top with shredded parmesan and serve with the garlic toast.
tips: Save parmesan rinds in a bag in the freezer. One rind adds a lot of savory flavor to a soup.
Spinach works instead of kale. Stir it in for the last 5 min; it wilts faster.
Use hot Italian sausage, or add ¼ tsp red pepper flakes, if you like heat.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months (the beans soften a little). Reheat on the stove over medium heat until it simmers, adding a splash of broth if it has thickened.

recipes.title: Seared Ahi Tuna Bowls

items: 2 sushi-grade ahi tuna steaks (6 oz each, about 1 inch thick)
3 Tbsp sesame seeds (white, black or mixed)
1 Tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)
2 cups cooked white rice, warm, or 4 cups mixed greens

steps: Buy tuna sold as sushi-grade or for raw eating, since the center stays rare. Keep it in the fridge until you're ready to cook.
Stir the mayo and sriracha in a small bowl. Prep the edamame, avocado, cucumber, carrot and scallions.
Pat the tuna dry with paper towels. Brush all sides with soy sauce, then press both flat sides into the sesame seeds on a plate.
Heat a heavy skillet over high heat until very hot, about 3 min. Add the oil and swirl.
Sear the tuna 45–60 sec per side, until the seeds are golden and only a thin outer band turns opaque. The center should stay deep pink.
Move to a cutting board and slice ¼ inch thick with a sharp knife.
Divide the rice or greens between 2 bowls. Add the vegetables and tuna, then drizzle the spicy mayo in lines.
tips: Keep the tuna cold right up to searing. A cold center stays rare while the outside browns.
If the sesame seeds darken before 45 sec, lower the heat to medium-high.
Prefer it cooked through? Sear 2–3 min per side to 145°F. It will be firmer and drier.
recipes.storage: Best eaten right away. Seared tuna keeps 1 day in the fridge at most. Eat it cold and don't reheat it. Store the vegetables and spicy mayo separately up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Shakshuka with Garlic Toast

items: ½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 Tbsp chopped fresh cilantro or parsley

steps: Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, pepper and a pinch of salt and cook 8–10 min, stirring now and then, until soft and the onion is golden at the edges.
Add the minced garlic, cumin and paprika and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes, add ½ tsp salt and a few grinds of pepper and bring to a simmer. Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer 10 min, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.

Meanwhile, set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler and turn the broiler to high. Mix the butter with the grated garlic and a pinch of salt, spread it on the bread and lay the slices on the sheet pan.

Make 5 wells in the sauce with a spoon. Crack each egg into the small cup, slide it into a well and sprinkle with a little salt. Cover and cook over medium-low heat 5–8 min, until the whites are fully set and opaque and the yolks are still soft.
While the eggs cook, broil the bread 1–2 min per side, until golden at the edges. Watch it, since it burns fast.
Scatter the feta and herbs over the skillet. Serve from the pan with the garlic toast for dipping.
tips: For firm yolks, cook covered 10–12 min, until the yolks no longer jiggle.
Make the sauce through step 3 up to 3 days ahead. Rewarm it in the skillet until bubbling before adding the eggs.
If the whites stay clear on top, spoon a little hot sauce over them and cover for 1 more min.
recipes.storage: The sauce keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. Cooked eggs don't reheat well, so rewarm the sauce until bubbling and cook fresh eggs in it. The toast is best fresh.

recipes.title: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas

items: 1½ lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into ½-inch strips
3 bell peppers (any color), sliced ¼ inch thick
1 large yellow onion, sliced ¼ inch thick
8 small flour tortillas (or 3 cups cooked rice)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper third. Line the sheet pan with parchment.
In the large bowl, toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil, spices and salt until evenly coated.
Spread everything in a single layer. Use 2 pans if it's crowded, or the vegetables will steam instead of brown.
Roast 20–25 min, stirring once halfway, until the vegetables are charred at the edges and the thickest strip of chicken reads 165°F.
For the last 10 min of roasting, wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them on a lower rack.
Squeeze the lime over the pan and toss. Serve in the warm tortillas or over rice with sour cream and avocado.
tips: For more char, broil the pan for the last 2 min, watching closely.
Chicken breast works too. Check it at 18 min, since it dries out faster.
Cut the chicken and vegetables to the same thickness so they finish at the same time.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days in a sealed container. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat or in the microwave until the chicken is hot (165°F).

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
recipes.cook: 8 hr on low or 4 hr on high
recipes.total: 8 hr 40 min on low (4 hr 40 min on high)

items: 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast, cut into 1½-inch cubes
1 cup dry red wine (or 1 more cup broth plus 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar)
1 lb carrots, peeled and cut into 1½-inch chunks

steps: Toss the beef with the flour, salt and pepper until coated. The flour helps it brown and thickens the stew later.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the beef in batches, 2 min per side, adding oil as needed. Don't crowd the pan, or the meat steams instead of browning. Move each batch to the slow cooker.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same skillet 3 min, then add the tomato paste and stir 1 min, until it darkens from red to brick.
Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom hard with a wooden spoon. Simmer 3–4 min, until reduced by half, then pour it all into the slow cooker.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves. Set the carrots and potatoes on top, where they steam instead of sitting submerged.
Cover and cook on low 8 hr or high 4 hr without lifting the lid, until the beef is fork-tender. If it's still tough, it's undercooked; give it 45–60 min more.
Stir in the peas for the last 10 min. Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves, then taste and add salt.
tips: Buy a chuck roast and cube it yourself. Packaged stew meat is mixed scraps that cook unevenly.
Cut the carrots and potatoes at least 1½ inches. Smaller pieces break down and turn the stew pasty. Yukon golds hold their shape; red potatoes work too.

Too thin? Whisk 2 Tbsp cornstarch into ¼ cup cold water, stir it in and cook uncovered on high 15 min. Too thick? Add hot broth ½ cup at a time. Tastes flat? Add salt first, then 1 tsp red wine vinegar.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months; the potatoes get a little grainy. Reheat covered over medium-low heat, stirring, until bubbling, with a splash of broth if it's thick.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Birria Tacos
recipes.cook: 8 hr on low, plus 30 min for the tacos

items: 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast, trimmed of thick fat and cut into 4 large chunks
1½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
4 dried guajillo chiles and 2 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed (or 3 Tbsp chili powder)
1 medium white onion, half roughly chopped and half finely diced
1 tsp dried oregano (Mexican if you have it)
12 oz Oaxaca or low-moisture mozzarella cheese, shredded (about 3 cups)
Finely diced onion (the reserved half from above)

steps: Put the stemmed, seeded chiles in the heatproof bowl, cover with the 2 cups boiling water and soak 10–15 min, until soft and bendable. Drain and discard the water. If you're using chili powder, skip this step.
Blend the soaked chiles (or chili powder), chipotle, the roughly chopped onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, 1½ tsp salt and the broth on high 1–2 min, until completely smooth.
Season the beef with a little salt and put it in the slow cooker. Pour the sauce over it. Cover and cook on low 8 hr, until the beef falls apart when pressed with a fork (about 200°F inside).

Lift the beef onto a cutting board and shred it with 2 forks, discarding any fat. Skim the red fat from the top of the broth into a small bowl. Taste the broth and add salt if needed. Toss the meat with ½ cup broth.
Heat the skillet over medium heat. Dip a tortilla in the red fat, or quickly in the broth, and lay it in the pan. Cover half with about 2 Tbsp cheese and 2–3 Tbsp beef.
Cook 2–3 min, until the tortilla is crisp underneath and the cheese melts. Fold it closed and cook about 1 min per side, until crisp on both sides. Repeat, cooking 2–3 at a time if they fit.
Ladle the hot broth into small cups. Serve the tacos with the broth for dipping, plus diced onion, cilantro and lime wedges.
tips: Use a fully thawed roast. Frozen meat stays too cold for too long in a slow cooker.
For deeper flavor, sear the beef chunks in 1 Tbsp oil in a hot skillet 3–4 min per side before they go in.
No slow cooker: braise covered in a Dutch oven at 325°F for 3–3½ hr, until it falls apart.
recipes.storage: Store the meat and broth separately. Fridge up to 4 days or freezer up to 3 months. Reheat the broth in a pot until simmering and the meat in a covered skillet with a splash of broth. Make the tacos fresh.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Braised Country-Style Ribs
recipes.cook: 6–7 hr on low, plus 25 min to finish

items: 3 lb bone-in country-style pork ribs (or beef short ribs)
¾ tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth (beef broth for short ribs)

steps: Pat the ribs completely dry. Mix the salt, pepper, smoked paprika and garlic powder, rub it all over the meat, and let it sit at room temperature up to 20 min while you heat the pan.

Heat the oil in a heavy 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the ribs in batches, about 3 min per side, until deeply browned. Don't crowd the pan. Move them to the slow cooker.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same skillet about 5 min, until softened. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 min, until the paste darkens.
Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Whisk in the vinegar, Worcestershire, brown sugar and Dijon, bring to a simmer and pour over the ribs. Tuck in the bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low until fork-tender: 6–7 hr for pork, 8–9 hr for beef short ribs. The meat should offer no resistance to a fork but not fall completely apart.
Move the ribs to a foil-lined rimmed sheet pan. Strain the cooking liquid into a medium saucepan and skim off the fat.

Simmer the liquid over medium-high heat about 12 min, until reduced by about a third. Stir the cornstarch into the cold water, whisk it in and simmer 1–2 min, until glossy. Taste and adjust the salt or vinegar.
Heat the broiler. Brush the ribs generously with sauce and broil 3–5 min, watching closely, until the edges caramelize and blister. Serve with the rest of the sauce.
tips: Searing and the final broil are what keep this from tasting like generic slow-cooker meat. Don't skip them.
Keep the liquid low. The ribs should sit in it, not swim, or the sauce comes out thin.
For a barbecue version, swap half the broth for 1 cup of your favorite barbecue sauce and cut the brown sugar in half.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days in the sauce. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat covered, in the sauce, in a 300°F oven until hot.

assumptions: Used bone-in pork country-style ribs, about 20 percent bone, giving roughly 1,090 g of edible raw meat.
About a quarter of the meat's fat and half the searing oil were assumed to render out and be skimmed from the cooking liquid.
Onion and garlic are strained out, so only about half of the onion's carbs and sugar were counted as staying in the sauce.
Kosher salt was estimated at about 1,280 mg sodium per teaspoon, roughly between Diamond Crystal and Morton.
Sodium uses low-sodium chicken broth at about 140 mg per cup plus typical Worcestershire and Dijon values, and assumes no extra salt is added at the end.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Cajun Jambalaya
recipes.cook: 6 hr on low, plus 30 min to finish
equipment: Medium saucepan with a lid (for the rice)

items: 12–14 oz andouille sausage, sliced into ¼-inch coins (or smoked kielbasa plus extra Cajun seasoning)
1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 (14.5-oz) can diced tomatoes, with their juice
2 Tbsp Cajun or Creole seasoning (salt-free if you can find it)
1 lb large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, thawed if frozen

steps: Brown the andouille in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat 4–5 min. Move it to the slow cooker, leaving the drippings in the pan.
Cook the chicken in the drippings 3–4 min, just to color it, and add it to the slow cooker. It finishes cooking there.
In the same pan, cook the onion, bell pepper and celery 4–5 min, until softened. Add the garlic for 30 seconds and the tomato paste for 1 min, then scrape it all into the slow cooker.
Stir in the tomatoes, broth, Cajun seasoning, thyme, oregano, bay leaves, Worcestershire and hot sauce. Cover and cook on low 6 hr (or high 3–4 hr), until the chicken is tender and reads 165°F.
About 30 min before the end, cook the rice on the stove or in a rice cooker as the package directs. Don't cook it in the slow cooker, where it turns to mush.
Stir in the shrimp, switch to high, cover and cook 15–30 min, until the shrimp are pink, opaque and curled into a loose C. A tight O means they're overcooked.

Remove the bay leaves. Taste before adding salt, since the seasoning and sausage are already salty. Stir 2–4 cups of the rice into the pot or spoon the jambalaya over rice, and top with green onions and parsley.
tips: To freeze some, set that portion aside before adding the shrimp. The base freezes well for 3 months, but shrimp turn rubbery.
Too salty? Stir in more broth and unsalted tomatoes. Too spicy? Stir in more rice.
Serve with cornbread or crusty French bread and a green salad with a vinegar dressing.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days, since the shrimp shorten its life. Refrigerate within 2 hr of cooking. Reheat on the stove with a splash of broth just until hot, so the shrimp don't toughen.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Chicken Adobo

items: 2½–3 lb bone-in skin-on chicken thighs (or thighs and drumsticks), fully thawed
½ cup vinegar (Filipino cane vinegar, white vinegar or apple cider vinegar)
1 tsp whole black peppercorns, lightly crushed

steps: Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and cook the thighs skin side down 5–6 min, until golden.
Set the chicken in the slow cooker skin side up. Stir together the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, brown sugar and water, and pour it over the chicken.
Cover and cook on low 4–5 hr, until the thickest thigh reads at least 175°F and is tender but not falling apart.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil, set the thighs on it skin side up, and broil 3–5 min, until the skin crisps.
Skim the fat from the cooking liquid and pour it into a medium saucepan. Simmer over medium heat 8–10 min, until reduced by about half and slightly syrupy. Remove the bay leaves.
Serve the chicken over rice with the sauce spooned over it, and top with green onions.
tips: For more flavor, marinate the chicken in the sauce in a zip-top bag in the fridge 1–8 hr. Pat it dry before browning and use the marinade as the sauce.
Too sour? Simmer the sauce a few minutes longer and add a little more sugar. Too salty? Thin it with water, and use low-sodium soy next time.
Leftovers make great adobo fried rice: chop the meat and stir-fry it with day-old rice, garlic and a spoonful of the sauce.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days; adobo tastes even better on day 2. Freezer up to 3 months in the sauce. Reheat covered over medium-low heat until it reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Chicken Cacciatore

items: 3 lb bone-in chicken thighs (6–8), fully thawed
2 Tbsp all-purpose flour, optional, to help thicken the sauce
½ cup dry red wine (or ½ cup chicken broth plus 1 Tbsp red wine vinegar)
½ tsp red pepper flakes, optional
½ cup Kalamata or black olives
¼ cup chopped fresh basil or parsley

steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with flour, if using.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken skin side down 5 min, until golden, then flip and cook 2 min more. Move to a plate. Pull off the skin now if you don't want it soft.
In the same pan, cook the onion, peppers and mushrooms 4–5 min, until they start to soften. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomato paste for 1 min.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble 1 min.
Scrape the vegetables into the slow cooker. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, pepper flakes and bay leaf, then nestle the chicken into the sauce.
Cover and cook on low 5–6 hr. Stir in the olives and capers for the last 30 min so they keep their texture. It's done when the meat comes easily off the bone and reads at least 175°F.
Skim the fat from the top. If the sauce is watery, cook uncovered on high 20–30 min. Remove the bay leaf, taste before adding salt since olives and capers are salty, and top with herbs and Parmesan.
tips: Serve over soft polenta, penne or pappardelle, or roasted potatoes, with crusty bread for the sauce.
Too acidic? Stir in a pinch of sugar or a small pat of butter.
Leftovers: pull the meat off the bone, chop it and toss it with pasta and the sauce.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days; it tastes even better the next day. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat covered over medium-low heat until it reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Slow-Cooker Chicken Vegetable Soup
recipes.cook: 6 hr 30 min to 7 hr 30 min (low, then high)

items: 1½ lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed
3 medium carrots, peeled and sliced ½ inch thick
2 celery ribs, sliced ½ inch thick
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes, with juice
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 cups dry wide egg noodles (about 3 oz)
3 cups baby spinach or chopped kale, stems removed (about 3 oz)

steps: Put the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, tomatoes with their juice, broth, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper in the slow cooker and stir.
Nestle the chicken thighs into the liquid so they're covered. Use thawed chicken only; frozen chicken stays too long at unsafe temperatures in a slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low 6–7 hr, until the carrots are tender and the chicken reads at least 165°F in the thickest part. It will be very tender.
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board, shred it into bite-size pieces with 2 forks and return it to the pot.
Turn the slow cooker to high. Stir in the noodles, cover and cook 20–30 min, until the noodles are tender.
Stir in the spinach for the last 5 min, or the kale for the last 10 min, until wilted. Taste and add salt and pepper.
tips: Leftover turkey: skip the raw chicken and cook the vegetables and broth on low 6 hr. Stir in 3–4 cups chopped cooked turkey with the noodles so it doesn't turn stringy, and heat until it reads 165°F.
Noodles soak up broth as they sit. If you want leftovers, cook the noodles separately and add them to each bowl.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freeze up to 3 months, ideally without the noodles. Reheat in a pot over medium heat until it boils, adding broth or water since the noodles absorb liquid.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs

items: 2–3 lb chicken thighs (6–8 bone-in skin-on, or 8–10 boneless skinless), fully thawed
1 Tbsp neutral oil, for searing bone-in thighs
1 Tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 Tbsp cold water

steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
For bone-in skin-on thighs, heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and cook them skin side down 5 min, until browned and some fat has rendered. Skip this for boneless thighs.
Whisk the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, garlic, vinegar, pepper flakes and ginger in a bowl.
Arrange the thighs in the slow cooker skin side up, in a single layer if you can, and pour the sauce over them.
Cover and cook on low 4–5 hr for bone-in or 3–4 hr for boneless, until the thickest thigh reads at least 175°F and the meat is tender but not falling off the bone.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and set the thighs on it, skin side up.
Pour the cooking liquid into a small saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Whisk in the cornstarch mixture and stir 2–3 min, until glossy and thick.
Brush the thighs with sauce and broil 3–4 min, until bubbly and caramelized. Watch closely, since honey burns fast. Spoon more sauce over the chicken and top with green onions and sesame seeds.
tips: Use thighs. If you must use breasts, cook on low only 2½–3 hr and pull them at 165°F.
If the glaze starts to burn, move the rack lower and broil in 1–2 min bursts.
Serve over white or jasmine rice with steamed broccoli or green beans. Leftovers are good chopped into rice bowls or lettuce wraps.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days with some of the sauce. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat in a covered skillet with a splash of water, or in a 350°F oven 10–15 min, until it reaches 165°F.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Italian Sausage and Peppers

items: 2 lb sweet Italian sausage links (or hot, or half and half)
3 bell peppers (1 green, 1 red, 1 yellow), sliced ½ inch thick
2 large yellow onions, halved and sliced ½ inch thick from root to tip

steps: Heat a griddle or 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat (375–400°F). Lay the sausages down with space between them. Cook 2 min per side, rolling a quarter turn each time, until all 4 sides are a deep chestnut brown, about 8 min total. If using a skillet, work in 2 batches so they brown instead of steam. They do not need to be cooked through.
Move the sausages to a plate and turn off the heat. Pour the ½ cup water onto the browned spots and scrape with a metal spatula while it bubbles. Pour the liquid into the slow cooker.
Spread the peppers, onions and garlic in the bottom of the slow cooker. Set the sausages on top.

In a medium bowl, stir the tomato paste, oregano, basil, red pepper flakes, salt and black pepper into the crushed tomatoes. Pour the sauce over the sausages. Do not add any other liquid; the vegetables release plenty.

Cover and cook on high for 3 hr without stirring or lifting the lid, until the peppers are tender but still hold their shape and the sausages read 160°F inside. If the sauce looks thin, prop the lid open a crack for the last 20 min.

Near the end of cooking, set an oven rack about 6 inches from the broiler and heat the broiler to high. Pull some bread out of the top half of each roll to make a shallow boat. Butter the cut sides, set the rolls cut side up on a rimmed baking sheet and broil 60–90 sec until golden.

Slice the sausages into coins or leave them whole. Fill the rolls with sausage, peppers, onions and sauce, then top each with a slice of provolone. Broil about 2 min, until the cheese melts and bubbles. Serve right away.
tips: Keep the peppers at least ½ inch thick and use yellow onions; thin strips turn to mush and sweet or red onions change the sauce.
Skip the rolls and serve over soft polenta with parmesan, rice or rigatoni, or in bowls with crusty bread and a sharp salad.
To char the vegetables first, cut them ¾ inch thick, sear them on the griddle and cut the slow cooker time to 2 hr on high.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate the sausage and peppers in an airtight container up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat in a covered pot over medium-low heat, stirring gently, until steaming and 165°F. Assemble sandwiches fresh.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Korean Braised Short Ribs

items: 3–4 lb bone-in English-cut short ribs (2- to 3-inch pieces)
¼ cup mirin (or 3 Tbsp rice vinegar plus 1 Tbsp sugar)
1 small Asian pear, peeled and grated (or 1 apple, grated)
½ cup water or beef broth
3 carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks
1 lb daikon radish, peeled and cut into 2-inch chunks (or 1 lb baby potatoes)
6 dried shiitake mushrooms, optional, soaked in hot water 20 min and stemmed
1 Tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 Tbsp cold water, optional

steps: Put the ribs in a large pot, cover with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil 5 min, then drain, rinse off the gray foam and pat dry. This is optional, but it gives a cleaner, less greasy sauce.
Whisk all the braising sauce ingredients in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the ribs in batches, 2–3 min per side, until browned. Leave space between pieces so they brown instead of steam.
Put the carrots, daikon, onion and mushrooms in the slow cooker. Set the ribs on top and pour the sauce over everything.

Cover and cook on low 7–8 hr, until the meat pulls away from the bone and a fork slides in easily, but the pieces still hold together. If it still feels firm, cook 30–60 min more; short ribs only get more tender with time.
Gently lift the meat and vegetables onto a platter and tent with foil. Tilt the slow cooker and skim off the fat. There will be a lot, and a fat separator makes it easy.
Pour the liquid into a medium saucepan and simmer over medium heat 8–10 min, until glossy and slightly syrupy. For a thicker sauce, whisk in the cornstarch mixture and simmer 2 min more.
Spoon the sauce over the ribs and vegetables, top with green onions and sesame seeds, and serve with steamed short-grain rice.
tips: Best made a day ahead. Chill it overnight, lift off the hardened fat, and reheat gently on the stove or on low in the slow cooker.
Too sweet? Add a splash of rice vinegar or a squeeze of lemon. Too salty? Thin the sauce with water.
Serve with kimchi, a quick cucumber salad or garlicky sautéed spinach. Leftover sauce over rice with a fried egg makes a good lunch.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, stored in the sauce. Freezer up to 3 months; the daikon softens a little. Reheat covered over low heat with a splash of water until hot.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Sticky Asian Pork Ribs

items: 3 lb baby back ribs (1 large or 2 small racks)

steps: On the bone side of each rack, slide a butter knife under the thin, shiny membrane at one end. Grip it with a paper towel and pull it off.
Cut the racks into sections of 3–4 ribs. Mix the rub and press it all over the ribs.
Whisk the sauce ingredients. Pour half into a container and refrigerate it for glazing at the end, so it never touches raw meat.
Stand the rib sections on their edges around the inside wall of the slow cooker, meaty side facing out. Pour the other half of the sauce over them. Don't add any other liquid.
Cover and cook on low 6–7 hr, until the meat has shrunk back about ½ inch from the bone ends and a bone wiggles when you twist it.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil and carefully move the ribs onto it, meat side up, with tongs and a spatula.
For extra glaze, skim the fat from the cooking liquid and simmer ½ cup of it with the reserved sauce in a small saucepan 3–5 min, until thick.

Brush the ribs generously with the reserved sauce and broil 3–5 min, until bubbly and charred at the edges. Brush again and broil 1–2 min more. Rest 5 min, cut between the bones and top with green onions and sesame seeds.
tips: If the meat falls off the bone, they cooked too long. Still tasty, but check at 5½–6 hr next time.
Broil in short bursts and move the rack lower if the glaze starts to burn.
Serve with jasmine or fried rice and an Asian slaw, smashed cucumber salad or corn on the cob.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat wrapped in foil in a 300°F oven 15–20 min, then unwrap and broil 1–2 min to crisp the glaze.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Teriyaki London Broil

items: 2–3 lb top round London broil, about 1½–2 inches thick
¼ cup mirin (or 3 Tbsp rice vinegar plus 1 Tbsp sugar)
¼ cup sake (or dry sherry, dry white wine or more broth)
¼ cup beef broth or water
1 Tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 Tbsp cold water
Red pepper flakes or sriracha, to taste, optional

steps: Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, broth and sesame oil in a bowl until the sugar dissolves.

Pat the beef dry and season with pepper. Skip salt, since the soy brings plenty. Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, then sear 2–3 min per side and a few seconds on the edges, until deeply browned.
Pour about ¼ cup of the sauce into the hot pan and scrape up the browned bits for 30 seconds. Pour it into the slow cooker.
Put the beef in the slow cooker and pour the rest of the sauce over it. Cover and cook on low 4½–5 hr, flipping once halfway if you can.

Check it at 4 hr the first time, since slow cookers vary. It's ready when a fork goes in with slight resistance and the meat holds together when lifted. If it feels tight and springy, give it 30 min more.
Move the beef to a cutting board, tent with foil and rest 10–15 min.
Meanwhile, strain the liquid into a small saucepan and skim off the fat. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisk in the cornstarch mixture and stir 2–3 min, until glossy and it coats a spoon.
Slice across the grain ⅛–¼ inch thick, at a slight angle. Fan the slices on a platter, spoon the glaze over them and top with green onions and sesame seeds. Serve the extra sauce on the side.
tips: For more flavor, marinate the beef in half the sauce in a zip-top bag in the fridge 2–8 hr (no more than 12). Wipe off the marinade before searing so the sugar doesn't burn.
Slicing thin across the grain matters more than anything else for tender top round. If it's tough, slice thinner or give it 30–60 min more next time.
Serve with white or jasmine rice and steamed broccoli, snap peas or bok choy. Leftovers make good rice bowls or teriyaki beef sandwiches.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the slices stored in the sauce so they don't dry out. Freezer up to 3 months, sliced, in sauce. Reheat gently in a covered skillet with a splash of water; full-power microwaving makes lean beef rubbery.

recipes.title: Southwest Chicken Chopped Salad

items: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
1½ cups corn kernels (frozen and thawed, or canned and drained)
2 bell peppers (red, yellow or orange), diced
¼ cup fresh lime juice (2 limes)

steps: Put the chicken between 2 sheets of plastic wrap. Pound the thick end with a meat mallet or rolling pin until it's an even ¾ inch thick, so it cooks through without drying out.
Mix the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and ¾ tsp salt and sprinkle it all over the chicken.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the chicken and cook 5–6 min without moving, until browned. Flip, lower the heat to medium and cook 4–6 min more, until it reads 165°F in the thickest part.
Move to a cutting board and rest 5 min, then slice ½ inch thick.
While the chicken cooks, whisk the lime juice, oil, honey, cilantro and salt in a small bowl.
In a large bowl, toss the beans, corn, peppers, onion, tomatoes and cilantro with most of the dressing.
Divide among 4 bowls, top with the sliced chicken and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.
tips: Boneless thighs stay juicier and need no pounding. Cook them 5–6 min per side to 165°F.
For meal prep, keep the dressing in a separate jar and toss just before eating.
Add diced avocado or crushed tortilla chips right before serving.
recipes.storage: Undressed salad and chicken keep in the fridge up to 4 days. Once dressed, eat it within 1 day. Serve the chicken cold or warm it in the microwave 30–60 sec.

recipes.title: Spaghetti and Homemade Meatballs

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
In a large bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in the milk 5 min. Add the beef, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper and mix gently with your hands just until combined. Overmixing makes them tough.
Roll into 1½-inch balls (about 18) and set them 1 inch apart on the pan. Wet your hands if the mixture sticks.
Bake 15–18 min, until browned and the center of a meatball reads 160°F.
While they bake, bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 Tbsp salt. Warm the marinara in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the baked meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer over low heat 10 min, turning them once.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti until al dente. Save ½ cup of pasta water, drain, and toss the spaghetti with a few spoonfuls of sauce and a splash of the water.
Serve the spaghetti topped with meatballs, more sauce and lots of parmesan.
tips: Freeze extra baked meatballs on the sheet pan, then bag them. Simmer them from frozen in sauce, covered, about 20 min, until they reach 165°F.
For a browner crust, sear the baked meatballs in 1 Tbsp oil over medium-high heat 2–3 min before they go into the sauce.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days with the meatballs in the sauce; keep the spaghetti separate. Freeze meatballs in sauce up to 3 months. Reheat covered on the stove over medium-low heat until the meatballs reach 165°F.

recipes.title: Spinach and Cheese Breakfast Casserole

items: 1 Tbsp butter, plus 1 tsp for the dish
½ medium yellow onion, finely diced
2 cups packed fresh baby spinach, roughly chopped
2 cups frozen shredded hash browns, thawed

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Butter a 9×9-inch baking dish.
Melt 1 Tbsp butter in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4–5 min, until soft and translucent. Add the spinach and stir 1–2 min, just until wilted. Let it cool a few minutes.
Pat the thawed hash browns dry with paper towels and spread them in the dish. Scatter the onion and spinach on top.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until smooth. Pour it over the vegetables and sprinkle the cheese evenly on top.
Bake 45–55 min, until puffed and golden, the center no longer jiggles when you nudge the dish, and a thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Rest 10 min so it sets, then cut into 6 pieces.
tips: Using frozen chopped spinach? Thaw 5 oz, squeeze it very dry in a towel and skip the wilting.
Assemble it the night before, cover and refrigerate. Bake straight from the fridge and add 10–15 min.
In an 8×8-inch dish it sits deeper, so start checking at 55 min.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, covered. Reheat a piece in the microwave 60–90 sec, until hot in the center. Freeze single pieces, wrapped, up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

recipes.title: Steak Bites with Corn Salsa and Guacamole

items: 1 lb sirloin steak, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 Tbsp neutral oil (such as avocado or canola)
1½ cups corn kernels (frozen and thawed, or canned and drained)
1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained

steps: Make the salsa. In a medium bowl, toss the corn, beans, red pepper, onion, cilantro, 2 Tbsp lime juice and ½ tsp salt.
Make the guacamole. Halve and pit the avocados and scoop them into a second bowl. Mash with a fork, leaving it a little chunky. Stir in 1 Tbsp lime juice and ½ tsp salt.
Pat the steak cubes dry with paper towels. Dry meat browns and wet meat steams. Toss with the chili powder, ¾ tsp salt and the pepper.

Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke, about 3 min. Add the oil, then the steak in a single layer with space between pieces. Work in 2 batches if they don't fit.
Sear 1–2 min without moving, until a dark crust forms. Turn with tongs and cook 1–2 min more. Pull at 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140–145°F for medium. Rest 3 min.
Spoon the salsa onto plates, pile the steak bites on top and add a scoop of guacamole in the middle.
tips: Don't crowd the pan. Too many pieces at once drop the heat and the steak turns gray instead of brown.
Make the salsa up to 1 day ahead. Make the guacamole last so it stays green.
Swap the steak for shrimp. Sear 1–2 min per side, until pink and opaque.
recipes.storage: Steak and salsa keep in the fridge up to 3 days in separate containers. Reheat the steak in a hot skillet 1–2 min so it doesn't overcook. Guacamole browns within a day, so make only what you'll eat.

recipes.title: Steak Bites with Sweet Potato Fries

items: 1 lb top sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 medium sweet potatoes (about 1½ lb), scrubbed and cut into ½-inch-thick sticks
1 jalapeño, stemmed, seeded and roughly chopped
½ cup packed fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.

Pat the sweet potato sticks dry. In a bowl, toss them with the cornstarch until lightly dusted, then add the oil, paprika and salt and toss again. Spread them on the pan in a single layer with space between; use 2 pans if crowded.
Bake 25–30 min, flipping once halfway, until browned at the edges and tender inside. Let them sit on the pan 3–5 min to crisp.
While the fries bake, blend the ranch, jalapeño and cilantro until smooth and pale green. Chill until serving.
Pat the steak cubes dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in the skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke.
Add the steak in a single layer, in 2 batches if needed. Sear 1–2 min without moving, until a brown crust forms, then turn and cook 1–2 min more.

Return all the steak to the pan and lower the heat to medium. Add the butter and garlic and toss 1 min, until the garlic is fragrant and the steak is coated. Check a cube: 130–135°F for medium-rare, 140–145°F for medium.
Serve the steak bites with the fries and green dip.
tips: Air fryer fries: cook at 400°F for 14–18 min in a single layer, shaking the basket halfway.
Leave the jalapeño seeds in if you want the dip spicier.
recipes.storage: Steak and fries keep 3 days in the fridge, the dip 4 days. Re-crisp the fries in the air fryer at 400°F or the oven at 425°F for 4–6 min. Warm the steak in a skillet over medium heat 1–2 min so it doesn't overcook.

recipes.title: Steak Tacos

items: 2 cups shredded iceberg or romaine lettuce
1 cup shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese (4 oz)

steps: Pat the steak dry. In a small bowl, mix 1 Tbsp oil, the chili powder, cumin, garlic, lime zest, 1 Tbsp lime juice, salt and pepper. Rub it all over the steak and let it sit at room temperature 15–30 min.
Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke, about 3 min. Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil.

Scrape the garlic bits off the steak so they don't burn. Sear 3–5 min per side without moving it, until deeply browned. Check the thickest part: 130–135°F for medium-rare, 140–145°F for medium. Skirt steak is thinner, so check it after 3 min per side.
Move the steak to a cutting board and rest 5 min.
While it rests, warm the tortillas in the skillet over medium heat 20–30 sec per side, until soft and spotted. Wrap them in a clean towel.
Find the lines (the grain) running along the steak. Slice it ¼ inch thick across those lines. Squeeze the rest of the lime juice over the slices.
Fill each tortilla with steak and top with lettuce, tomato and cheese.
tips: Slicing across the grain is what makes flank steak tender. Sliced with the grain, it turns chewy.
For more flavor, marinate up to 8 hr in the fridge. Any longer and the lime makes the meat mushy.
Sirloin works too and often costs less. Cook it to the same temperatures.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the sliced steak in a skillet over medium heat 1–2 min, just until warm, so it doesn't overcook. Store the toppings separately.

recipes.title: Street Corn Pasta Salad

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
3 cups corn kernels (from about 4 ears, or frozen and thawed, patted dry)

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 1 Tbsp salt. Cook the rotini as the package says, until al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool, then shake off as much water as you can.

Heat the dry skillet over high heat 2 min. Add the corn in one layer and cook 3–4 min without stirring, until it browns in spots. Stir and cook 2–3 min more, until charred in several places. Sprinkle with ½ tsp salt and spread on a plate to cool 5 min.
Whisk the mayo, sour cream, lime juice and chili powder in the large bowl until smooth.
Add the pasta, corn, jalapeño, scallions, cilantro and ⅓ cup cotija. Toss until evenly coated. Taste and add salt or more lime juice.
Top with the extra cotija and a sprinkle of chili powder. Serve right away, or chill until serving.
tips: Add a can of drained black beans or diced cooked chicken to make it a full meal.
The pasta soaks up dressing as it sits. If making it ahead, hold back a third of the dressing and stir it in just before serving.
Can't find cotija? Feta works.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days in a sealed container. Stir in 1–2 Tbsp mayo or lime juice to loosen before serving. Don't freeze.

recipes.title: Sweet Potatoes with Spiced Ground Beef

items: 4 medium sweet potatoes (about 8 oz each), scrubbed
1 clove garlic, finely grated or minced

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil, since sweet potatoes drip a sticky syrup.
Prick each sweet potato several times with a fork and set it on the pan. Bake 45–60 min, until a knife slides in easily and the skins look puffed and wrinkled.
