Make the sauce: stir the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice and salt in a small bowl. Add water 1 Tbsp at a time until it drizzles off a spoon. Chill until serving.

About 15 min before the potatoes are done, heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook 6–8 min, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F. Spoon off all but about 1 Tbsp of fat.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Split each potato lengthwise and fluff the flesh with a fork. Spoon in the beef and drizzle with the garlic yogurt sauce.
tips: With bacon, the way she made it in March 2025: cook 4 slices in the skillet first until crisp, brown the beef in 1 Tbsp of the drippings, and crumble the bacon over the top.
Speed it up: microwave the pricked sweet potatoes 8–12 min, turning halfway, until tender.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the beef, potatoes and sauce stored separately. Reheat the beef and potatoes in the microwave until steaming hot (165°F). Serve the sauce cold; it keeps 4 days.

recipes.title: Taco Salad
equipment: Small zip-top bag (for the sour cream lines)

items: 1 lb lean ground beef (85–90% lean) or ground turkey
1 tsp neutral oil (only if using turkey)
1 large head romaine or iceberg lettuce (about 8 cups), shredded
1 cup guacamole, or 2 ripe avocados, diced

steps: Stir the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika and salt together in a small bowl.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the meat (and the oil if using turkey). Cook 6–8 min, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains. Beef should read 160°F and turkey 165°F.
Tip the pan and spoon off most of the fat. Lower the heat to medium. Stir in the seasoning and ¼ cup water and simmer 2–3 min, until the liquid is mostly gone and the meat looks glossy.
While the meat cooks, shred the lettuce and dice the tomatoes and avocado. Divide the lettuce among 4 plates or bowls.
Spoon the warm meat over the lettuce. Add the cheddar, tomatoes and guacamole or avocado.
Spoon the sour cream into a small zip-top bag, snip off a tiny corner and pipe it over each salad in lines. Serve with salsa on the side.
tips: Keep the meat and lettuce apart until you eat. Warm meat wilts lettuce fast.
Add crushed tortilla chips or a can of rinsed black beans for crunch and bulk.
Make a triple batch of the seasoning and keep it in a jar. Use 5 tsp per 1 lb of meat.
recipes.storage: Cooked meat keeps in the fridge up to 4 days or the freezer up to 3 months. Keep the lettuce and toppings separate. Reheat the meat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of water, or in the microwave, until hot. Assembled salads do not keep.

recipes.title: Thai Red Curry Squash Soup
equipment: Large pot or Dutch oven with lid

items: 1 small butternut squash (about 2½ lb), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes (about 6 cups)
1 (13.5 oz) can coconut milk, well shaken
½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
3 Tbsp coconut milk (saved from the can)

steps: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5–6 min, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 min.
Stir in the curry paste and cook 1 min, stirring, until fragrant and a shade darker.
Pour 3 Tbsp of the coconut milk into a small cup and save it for topping. Add the rest of the can, the squash, broth and salt to the pot.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn to medium-low, cover and simmer 20 min, until the squash mashes easily with a spoon.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. If using a countertop blender, fill it no more than halfway, remove the center cap and cover the hole with a folded towel so steam can escape.
Stir in lime juice a little at a time, and salt, to taste. Thin with a splash of broth if it's too thick.
Ladle into bowls. Swirl in the saved coconut milk and top with cilantro and pepitas.
tips: Curry paste brands vary in heat. Start with 2 Tbsp. You can stir in more after blending and simmer 2 min.
Stir in 1 tsp fish sauce with the lime for a deeper, saltier flavor.
Pre-cut squash from the store saves 10 min of peeling and chopping. Use 2 (20 oz) packages, about 6 cups.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 5 days or freezer up to 3 months, without toppings. Reheat in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until steaming. Coconut milk can separate, so stir well.

recipes.title: Tomato and Egg Scramble

items: ¼ tsp kosher salt, plus a pinch for the tomatoes
1 scallion, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate
2 cups cooked white rice, warm, or 2 slices toast

steps: Beat the eggs with ¼ tsp salt in a small bowl until no streaks of white remain.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs, let them sit 10 sec, then push them slowly from the edges to the center with a spatula.
When the eggs are mostly set but still a little wet and glossy, 1–2 min, slide them onto a plate. They finish cooking later.
Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil and the scallion whites to the pan over medium heat and stir 30 sec. Add the tomatoes, sugar, a pinch of salt and 2 Tbsp water.
Cook 3–5 min, stirring and pressing some tomatoes with the spatula, until they burst and turn saucy.
Return the eggs and fold gently 30–60 sec, until no runny egg remains and the eggs are coated in the tomato sauce.
Top with the scallion greens. Serve over rice or with toast.
tips: Pull the eggs early. They keep cooking in the hot tomatoes, and dry, rubbery eggs are the most common mistake here.
Only have regular tomatoes? Cut 2 into wedges and cook them 4–5 min.
Add 1 tsp soy sauce to the tomatoes for a more savory sauce.
recipes.storage: Best eaten right away. Leftovers keep 1 day in the fridge. Reheat in the microwave in 20-sec bursts, just until warm.

recipes.title: Tomato Soup with Cheesy Garlic Toast

items: 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 tsp sugar (to soften the tomatoes' acidity)
¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped (about 10 leaves)
4 thick slices (¾ inch) Italian bread or sourdough

steps: Melt the butter in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 6–8 min, stirring, until soft and golden at the edges. Add the garlic and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, broth, salt, pepper and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered 20 min, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.

During the last 5 min of simmering, set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler and heat the broiler on high. Mix the softened butter and garlic in a small bowl. Spread it on one side of each bread slice and set them butter side up on a rimmed sheet pan.
Broil 1–2 min, until the edges are golden. Top with the mozzarella and broil 1–3 min more, until bubbling and spotted brown. Watch closely; it burns fast. Cut each slice into 4 squares.

Turn off the heat under the soup. Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. With a countertop blender, fill it no more than halfway, take out the center cap, cover the hole with a folded towel and blend in batches.
Stir in the cream and basil and warm over low heat 2 min without boiling. Taste and add salt.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle each with 1 Tbsp parmesan and serve with the toast squares.
tips: No fresh basil: add 1 tsp dried basil with the tomatoes instead.
Fire-roasted crushed tomatoes give the soup a smoky flavor.
recipes.storage: Soup keeps in the fridge 4 days and freezes up to 3 months. Reheat over medium-low heat, stirring, without boiling. The toast is best fresh; re-crisp leftovers at 375°F for 5 min.

recipes.title: Turkish Eggs (Çılbır)
recipes.prep: 10 min (plus 20 min to take the chill off the yogurt)
equipment: Small saucepan or skillet (for the chili butter)

items: 1 Tbsp white vinegar (for the poaching water)
1 tsp Aleppo pepper (or ½ tsp paprika plus a pinch of red chili flakes)

steps: Take the yogurt out of the fridge 20 min early so it isn't cold. Stir in the garlic and salt, then spread it on 2 plates or shallow bowls.
Fill the medium saucepan with 3 inches of water, add the vinegar and bring it to a bare simmer over medium heat, with small bubbles but no rolling boil.
Crack each egg into the small cup. Stir the water to make a gentle swirl and slide the eggs in one at a time. Cook 3–4 min, until the whites are fully set and the yolks are still soft.
Lift the eggs out with the slotted spoon, let them drain 5 sec and set 2 on each plate of yogurt.
Melt the butter in the small pan over medium-low heat. When it foams, stir in the Aleppo pepper and take the pan off the heat after 15–20 sec, before it scorches.
Spoon the chili butter over the eggs and yogurt. Sprinkle with dill and serve with toast.
tips: To fry instead, cook the eggs in 1 tsp butter in a covered nonstick skillet over medium-low heat 3–4 min, until the whites are set.
Forgot to take the yogurt out? Microwave it 15–20 sec and stir. Cold yogurt cools the eggs fast.
Poach the eggs 2 at a time if your pan is small, so they don't run together.
recipes.storage: Doesn't keep. Eat it right away. The garlic yogurt alone keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Yogurt and Granola Bowls

items: 3 cups plain or vanilla Greek yogurt
1 cup nuts (almonds, pecans or walnuts), roughly chopped
¼ cup neutral oil or melted coconut oil

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
In a large bowl, stir the oats, nuts, cinnamon and salt. Add the maple syrup and oil and stir until every oat looks shiny and coated.
Spread it on the pan in an even layer and press it down firmly with the spatula.
Bake 12 min. Stir so the edges don't burn, press it flat again and bake 10–13 min more, until golden brown and fragrant. It will still feel a little soft.
Cool completely on the pan, at least 20 min, without touching it. It crisps and forms clusters as it cools. Break it into pieces.
For each bowl, spoon in ¾ cup yogurt and top with about ⅓ cup granola and a handful of berries or banana slices.
tips: Add the granola right before eating so it stays crunchy.
Watch the last 5 min of baking. Maple syrup goes from golden to burnt quickly.
Stir in ½ cup raisins or dried cranberries after baking, not before, or they burn.
recipes.storage: Granola keeps in an airtight jar at room temperature up to 2 weeks, or frozen up to 3 months. Build bowls just before eating, since they get soggy. Cut berries keep 2–3 days in the fridge. Slice banana fresh.

recipes.title: Barbecue Chicken Pizza

items: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts (1 large or 2 small)
¾ cup purchased barbecue sauce, for the marinade
½ cup purchased barbecue sauce, for the pizza, divided
½ medium red bell pepper, thinly sliced

steps: Lay the chicken between 2 sheets of plastic wrap and gently pound it with a meat mallet to an even ½-inch thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Put the chicken in a gallon zip-top bag with ¾ cup barbecue sauce, seal, and turn to coat. Refrigerate for 6 hr or overnight.
Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates. Lift the chicken out of the bag and discard the used marinade.

Grill the chicken for 4 to 6 min per side, until it has good grill marks and an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part. Pull it off as soon as it hits 165°F so it stays juicy. Let it rest 5 min, then cut it into bite-size pieces.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. If using a pizza stone, set it in the oven while it heats.
Spread ¼ cup barbecue sauce in a thin layer over the crust. Scatter the chicken evenly over the top, then add the mushrooms, red pepper and caramelized onions, if using.
Drizzle the remaining ¼ cup barbecue sauce over the toppings. Sprinkle the Monterey Jack cheese evenly to the edges.
Slide the pizza onto the hot stone or set it on the pizza pan. Bake for about 20 min, until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling and the chicken is hot.
Let the pizza rest 2 min, then cut it into 8 wedges and serve.
tips: Grill the chicken up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate it, so dinner night is just assembly and baking.
Don't reuse the raw-chicken marinade on the pizza. Use fresh sauce from the bottle.
Swap in smoked Gouda or cheddar for part of the Monterey Jack for a smokier flavor.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftover slices in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze wrapped slices for up to 2 months. Reheat in a 375°F oven or a covered skillet over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 min, until the cheese melts and the chicken is hot.

recipes.title: Big Ol' Mess
equipment: Foil cooking bag or heavy-duty aluminum foil

items: 1 lb smoked sausage, cut into 1-inch chunks
1 large green bell pepper, cut into bite-size chunks
1 large sweet onion, cut into bite-size chunks
1 loaf crusty bread, cut into chunks (optional)

steps: Heat the grill to medium, about 350°F to 400°F.
Put the sausage, jalapeños, green pepper and onion in the foil cooking bag and spread them into an even layer.
In a small bowl, stir the Tabasco sauce into the sweet-and-sour sauce until smooth. Pour it over the sausage and vegetables in the bag.
Fold and crimp the open edge of the bag tightly so no steam or sauce can escape.
Set the bag on the grill grate, close the lid, and cook about 45 min. Use long tongs to flip the bag carefully every 15 min so everything cooks evenly.

Move the bag to a heatproof platter. Cut a slit in the top, keeping your face back from the hot steam. The vegetables should be tender and the sausage should read 165°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Serve straight from the bag. For an appetizer, thread the sausage and vegetables onto skewers, or spoon them over chunks of crusty bread.
tips: No foil bag? Make a packet from two large sheets of heavy-duty foil and crimp all edges tightly.
For milder heat, seed the jalapeños or cut the Tabasco to 2 tbsp.
You can also bake the bag on a sheet pan at 400°F for about 45 min.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 3 days, or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat in a covered skillet over medium heat until hot, about 5 to 8 min.

recipes.title: Jerk Chicken Pizza with Mango Salsa
equipment: Large baking sheet or 12-inch pizza pan

items: ¼ cup grated Asiago cheese (about ¾ oz)
¼ cup shredded mozzarella cheese (about 1 oz)
¼ cup grated smoked mozzarella cheese (about 1 oz)
½ ripe mango, peeled and diced
1 tsp chopped fresh mint, basil, cilantro or a mix of all three

steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Set the pizza crust on a large baking sheet or 12-inch pizza pan.

Rub the jerk seasoning all over the chicken. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Cook the chicken 5 to 7 min per side, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F. Move it to a cutting board and let it rest 5 min.
Add the mushrooms to the same skillet and cook over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 min, stirring, until they soften. Tip out any liquid in the pan.
Slice the rested chicken into thin strips.
In a small mixing bowl, stir together the mango, red onion, tomato, 1 tbsp olive oil, balsamic vinegar and herbs until well mixed.
Spread the barbecue sauce over the crust, leaving a ½-inch border. Top with the mushrooms and chicken strips, then scatter the Asiago, mozzarella and smoked mozzarella over everything.
Bake 7 to 8 min, until the crust edges are browned and the cheese is golden and bubbling.
Spoon the mango salsa over the hot pizza right away, slice and serve.
tips: Pound the chicken breast to an even ¾-inch thickness so it cooks through without drying out.
Make the salsa up to 2 hr ahead and keep it chilled; stir before using.
Rotisserie chicken works in a pinch; toss the strips with the jerk seasoning instead of searing.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate leftover pizza up to 3 days and the salsa separately up to 2 days. Reheat slices on a baking sheet at 400°F for 6 to 8 min until hot. The pizza does not freeze well once topped with salsa.

recipes.title: John's Smoked Ribs

items: 2 racks pork baby back ribs (about 5 to 6 lb total)
¾ to 1 cup packed brown sugar
¼ tsp cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps: Set the ribs bone side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Slide a butter knife under the thin membrane on the back of each rack, grab it with a paper towel, and peel it off in one piece.
In a medium bowl, mix the ¾ to 1 cup brown sugar, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, oregano, dry mustard, cumin, cayenne and árbol chile until no clumps of sugar remain.
Rub the olive oil all over both racks. Press the rub generously onto every side of the ribs. Wrap each rack tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hr and up to 24 hr.
Start the smoker and bring it to 225°F, keeping it between 200°F and 250°F the whole cook. Unwrap the ribs and discard the plastic.
Place the ribs bone side down on the smoker grate. Smoke uncovered for 3 hr, until the surface is deep reddish brown and the rub has set into a dry crust.

Move the ribs to the baking sheet. Drizzle the honey over the meaty side and spread it evenly, then pat the ½ cup brown sugar over the honey. Wrap each rack tightly in a double layer of heavy-duty foil.

Return the wrapped ribs to the smoker and cook for at least 3 hr more, until an instant-read thermometer between the bones reads 195°F to 203°F and the probe slides in with almost no resistance. Pork is safe at 145°F, but ribs need the higher temperature to turn tender. Cook longer if you want them even softer.
Remove the ribs, rest them in the foil for 10 min, then unwrap carefully, watching for steam, and slice between the bones.
tips: Use spare ribs instead of baby backs if you like; add about 1 hr to the wrapped stage.
Mix the rub up to 1 month ahead and store it airtight at room temperature.
Check the smoker temperature every hour, since letting it climb past 250°F can burn the sugar in the rub.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate wrapped in foil up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat in foil in a 300°F oven for 20 to 30 min, until hot through.

recipes.title: Ronies Droney Tomato Macaroni and Cheese

items: ½ lb American cheese, torn into about 1-inch pieces
1 to 1½ cups milk or half-and-half (enough to just cover the cheese)

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat. Cook the macaroni until al dente, following the package time (usually 6 to 8 min), until tender but still firm to the bite. Drain in a colander and set aside.
Put the butter in the bottom of a 3-quart saucepan, then spread the torn cheese over it in an even layer.
Pour in enough milk or half-and-half to just cover the cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Set the pan over low heat. Stir every few min until the cheese is fully melted and the sauce is smooth, 8 to 12 min. Keep the heat low so the sauce doesn't boil or turn grainy.
Stir in the condensed tomato soup straight from the can. Keep stirring over low heat until the sauce is an even orange color and hot, 2 to 3 min.
Add the drained macaroni and stir to coat. Let it warm through over low heat, stirring now and then, 2 to 3 min. Taste, add more salt and pepper if needed, and serve hot.
tips: To feed a crowd, double or triple everything and use a larger pot.
Half-and-half makes a richer, creamier sauce than milk.
Any short pasta works in place of elbows, like shells or rotini.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat on the stove over low heat or in the microwave, stirring in a splash of milk to loosen the sauce. It doesn't freeze well because the sauce turns grainy.

recipes.title: Smoked Brisket Baked Beans
equipment: Smoker or grill set up for indirect heat

items: 1½ bottles Heath Riles BBQ Sweet BBQ Sauce, divided (1 bottle and ½ bottle)
½ bag (1 lb, about 2¼ cups packed) Domino light brown sugar
⅓ yellow bell pepper, finely diced
⅓ red bell pepper, finely diced
⅓ green bell pepper, finely diced
1 lb leftover smoked Texas-style brisket, cut into ½-inch chunks
1 to 3 tbsp Heath Riles BBQ Hot BBQ Rub, to taste

steps: Heat your smoker to 275°F to 300°F for indirect cooking. You can also use your oven at the same temperature.
Nest one aluminum pan inside the other for support. Pour the drained beans into the top pan.
Add 1 bottle of the BBQ sauce. Spread the brown sugar over the top, breaking up any clumps with a spoon. Add the onion and all 3 bell peppers, then stir until the sugar is mixed in.

Add the brisket chunks and sprinkle on the rub, using more for hotter beans. Pour the remaining ½ bottle of sauce over everything and stir well. If making ahead, cover tightly with foil and refrigerate up to 1 day.
Set the pan uncovered on the smoker grate and close the lid. Cook until the beans start to bubble around the edges, about 45 min to 1 hr, then stir well.

Keep cooking, stirring every 30 min, for about 5 hr total. The beans are done when they're dark and thick with just a little liquid, the onions and peppers are tender, and the center reads at least 165°F. For soupier beans, stop at about 3 hr.
Remove the pan from the smoker and give the beans a final stir. Let them rest 10 min so the sauce thickens slightly, then serve.
tips: No brisket? Use 1 lb browned ground beef (cooked to 160°F) or leftover pulled pork instead.
If you only have green bell pepper, use 1 whole green pepper in place of the 3 partial peppers.
Go easy on the rub at first. You can add more near the end, but you can't take it out.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 3 days, or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat covered in a 325°F oven or in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring and adding a splash of water if thick, until hot throughout (165°F).

recipes.title: Soy Ginger Steak-On-A-Stick Marinade
recipes.servings: About 3½ cups marinade (enough for 3 lb steak, 6 servings)

items: ½ cup packed dark brown sugar
3 tbsp fresh ginger, peeled and minced
3 lb flank, skirt or sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick

steps: Whisk the olive oil, soy sauce, molasses, brown sugar, mirin and dry mustard in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves, about 1 min.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, scallions, red pepper flakes and pineapple juice if using. Season with salt and pepper, going light on the salt since soy sauce is already salty.

Divide the steak between 2 gallon-size zip-top bags and pour the marinade over it. Press out the air, seal and refrigerate 4 to 12 hr, turning once. If you added pineapple juice, keep it to 8 hr or less so the meat doesn't turn mushy.

Take the steak out of the fridge 30 min before cooking. Heat the grill or grill pan over high heat to about 450°F. Lift the steak from the marinade, let the excess drip off and pat it dry. Throw out the used marinade.

Grill the steak 4 to 6 min per side, until well charred. Check with an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part: 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140–145°F for medium. Move it to a cooler spot if the sugars flare up or burn.
Rest the steak on a cutting board 5 to 10 min. Slice thinly against the grain and serve.
tips: Never reuse marinade that touched raw meat. Set aside ½ cup before adding the steak if you want some for drizzling.
The pineapple juice stretches the batch for more meat, but its enzymes soften steak fast, so watch the time.
This also works on chicken thighs or pork tenderloin. Cook chicken to 165°F and pork to 145°F with a 3 min rest.
recipes.storage: Unused marinade keeps in a sealed jar in the fridge up to 1 week or frozen up to 3 months. Cooked steak keeps in the fridge 3 to 4 days; reheat gently in a skillet over medium-low heat or eat it cold on salads.

recipes.title: Roasted Honeynut Squash

items: 2 honeynut squash (about 1 lb each), halved lengthwise and seeded

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment or foil.
Cut each squash in half lengthwise from stem to blossom end. Scoop out the seeds and stringy bits with a spoon. Keep the skin on; it's thin and edible.
Brush the cut sides with the olive oil. Sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Set the halves cut-side down on the pan. Roast 20 to 25 min, until the cut faces are deep golden brown and caramelized underneath.

Flip the halves cut-side up. Put 1 piece of butter in each cavity and drizzle in the maple syrup, if using. Roast 5 to 10 min more, until the butter melts and a fork slides through the thick neck with no resistance.
Serve 1 half per person. Scoop the flesh from the shell with a spoon, or eat the skin too.
tips: Check doneness at the thick neck, since it softens last. Small squash may be done 5 min early.
For cubes, cut the squash into 1-inch chunks with the skin on, toss with the oil, salt and pepper, and roast at 425°F for 20 to 25 min, flipping halfway.
For a savory version, skip the maple and add a pinch of smoked paprika or some chopped fresh sage to the butter.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 4 days. Reheat at 375°F for 10 to 15 min or microwave until hot. To freeze, scoop out the flesh and freeze up to 3 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat.

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Summer Vegetables

items: 2 red bell peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium eggplant, peeled and cut into ¾-inch pieces
1 medium zucchini, cut into ¾-inch pieces
1 medium red onion, sliced ¼ inch thick
2 lb sweet Italian sausage links (about 8 links), left whole
1 (12-oz) package cherry tomatoes (about 2 cups), left whole

steps: Set oven racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven. Put 2 rimmed sheet pans on the racks and preheat the oven to 425°F with the pans inside.
In a large bowl, add the bell peppers, eggplant, zucchini and red onion. Pour the olive oil over them, then sprinkle with the Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Toss until every piece is coated.

Using oven mitts, pull out the hot pans and split the vegetables between them in a single layer. Tuck the sausages in among the vegetables, about 4 per pan. The vegetables should sizzle when they hit the pan.
Roast for 15 min. Take the pans out, toss the vegetables and turn the sausages, then scatter the cherry tomatoes over both pans. Return the pans to the oven, switching their rack positions.

Roast 15 to 20 min more, until the sausages are browned and register 160°F inside on an instant-read thermometer, the vegetables are tender with browned edges, and the tomatoes are blistered and starting to burst.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar lightly over the sausage and vegetables on the pans. Move everything to a large platter, spooning the pan juices over the top.
Sprinkle with the basil. Serve hot with the crusty bread for soaking up the juices and the grainy mustard on the side.
tips: Hot Italian, chicken or turkey sausage all work; fully cooked sausage such as kielbasa only needs to heat through to 165°F, so check it early.
Chop the vegetables up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge until you roast.
Keep the vegetables in a single layer with space between pieces so they brown instead of steam.
recipes.storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months; the vegetables soften after freezing. Reheat on a sheet pan at 400°F for 10 to 12 min, or in the microwave, until the sausage reaches 165°F.

assumptions: The recipe makes 4 to 6 servings, so the totals were divided by the middle value of 5.
All sausage fat and the olive oil are counted because the pan juices are spooned over the platter.
The crusty bread is assumed to be a 1 lb loaf of French-style bread, and all of it plus the mustard is included.
The 2 tsp of kosher salt is estimated at about 3,000 mg sodium total, between Diamond Crystal and Morton values.
Sausage sodium and fat vary by brand; values use typical USDA raw sweet Italian pork sausage, and balsamic is figured at 1.5 Tbsp.
